nodes.definition: Двухфазный (α+β) титановый сплав с 6% алюминия и 4% ванадия, сочетающий высокую прочность, коррозионную стойкость и биосовместимость, широко применяемый в авиации и медицинских имплантатах.

Механическая характеристика жёсткости материала, определяемая как отношение нормального напряжения к соответствующей деформации в упругой области. Регулирование модуля упругости в ячеистых структурах важно для создания имплантатов с требуемой жёсткостью.
Доля объёма пустот в материале, выраженная в процентах. Пористость существенно влияет на модуль упругости и механические свойства ячеистых титановых конструкций.

Свойство материала проявлять различное поведение в зависимости от направления приложения нагрузки. Ячеистые структуры с контролируемой анизотропией позволяют адаптировать имплантат под направленные нагрузки.

Численный метод решения инженерных задач, заключающийся в дискретизации расчётной области на элементы и аппроксимации искомых полей; в работе применён для моделирования напряжённо-деформированного состояния ячеистых структур.
Стандартизированный метод определения механических характеристик ячеистых материалов путём одноосного сжатия согласно ISO 13314:2011.

Группа технологий послойного построения трёхмерного объекта по цифровой модели, включающая селективное лазерное плавление (SLM), электронно-лучевое плавление (EBM) и прямое энергетическое осаждение (DED).
Хирургические устройства, вживляемые в организм, где титановые сплавы с контролируемой пористой архитектурой и анизотропией модуля упругости обеспечивают остеоинтеграцию и биосовместимость.
Химический элемент (Ti) — лёгкий, прочный, коррозионностойкий металл. Порошок титана используется в аддитивных технологиях для производства деталей.
nodes.name: Titanium

nodes.definition: Диоксид титана — твёрдый белый порошок, используемый в качестве прекурсора для алюмотермического восстановления с получением металлического титана.
Метод получения металлического порошка путём распыления струи расплава потоком инертного газа (аргона или гелия), широко применяемый в производстве титановых порошков.
Метод получения сферических порошков с помощью плазменных горелок, которые расплавляют и диспергируют металл, обеспечивая высокую чистоту и узкое распределение частиц по размерам.
Метод получения порошков, при котором вращающийся титановый электрод оплавляется плазменной дугой, а капли расплава, срываясь под действием центробежной силы, затвердевают в сферические частицы.
Многостадийный способ производства порошка, при котором титановую губку (получаемую восстановлением TiCl4 магнием) измельчают и рассеивают по фракциям; реализован на «ВСМПО-АВИСМА».
Метод получения титанового порошка путём восстановления TiO2 алюминием при 1150 °C в вакууме. В результате образуются гранулы титана и корунд (Al2O3).

Метод очистки поверхностей, основанный на эффекте кавитации: в жидкости под действием ультразвука возникают пузырьки, схлопывание которых создаёт ударные волны, отделяющие загрязнения (например, корунд от титановых гранул).

Характеристика порошка, отражающая долю частиц различных размеров во фракции. Правильное соотношение фракций обеспечивает высокую плотность упаковки и улучшает технологические свойства при аддитивном производстве.
Способность порошка равномерно и стабильно растекаться, критически важная для процессов аддитивного производства, где равномерное нанесение слоя влияет на качество детали.
Массовая доля кислорода в титановом порошке; повышенное содержание кислорода охрупчивает титан и ухудшает механические свойства конечных изделий.

Явление образования и последующего схлопывания парогазовых пузырьков в жидкости под действием ультразвука, сопровождающееся высвобождением энергии и ударными волнами. Используется для ультразвуковой очистки поверхности.
nodes.name: Cavitation

nodes.definition: Среда с пониженным давлением, используемая при алюмотермическом восстановлении TiO2 для предотвращения окисления титана при высокой температуре.
Температура, при которой проводят алюмотермическое восстановление TiO2 алюминием в вакууме для получения титановых гранул.
Аддитивная технология, в которой лазерный луч избирательно расплавляет порошковый материал слой за слоем для создания плотных металлических деталей.
Аддитивная технология, использующая мощный электронный луч для послойного плавления металлического порошка в вакууме, применяемая для титановых сплавов.
Аддитивный процесс, в котором сфокусированная тепловая энергия (лазер, плазма или дуга) расплавляет материал непосредственно в зоне построения, обеспечивая высокую производительность.

Аддитивная технология, при которой порошковые частицы (0.01–50 мкм) ускоряются в сверхзвуковом холодном или подогретом газовом потоке (0.4–0.7 Тпл) и осаждаются на подложку без плавления, обеспечивая покрытия с высокой адгезией (до 120 МПа) и низкой пористостью.
Способность покрытия сохранять механическую связь с подложкой, количественно характеризуемая напряжением, необходимым для отделения покрытия; ключевой параметр надёжности напылённых слоёв.

Метод получения изображений с высоким разрешением путём сканирования поверхности сфокусированным пучком электронов и регистрации вторичных или отражённых электронов, широко используемый для анализа микроструктуры и морфологии материалов.

Биоинертное покрытие на основе β-фазного сплава титана и тантала, наносимое электровзрывным напылением, отличающееся низким модулем упругости и наноструктурированной поверхностью; предназначено для улучшения остеоинтеграции титановых имплантатов.

Импульсный плазменный метод нанесения покрытий, при котором поверхность частично переплавляется и затвердевает с высокой скоростью охлаждения, что позволяет формировать наноструктурированные биоинертные покрытия с низким модулем упругости (например, системы Ti-Ta) на медицинских имплантатах.

Титановые сплавы с преобладающей β-фазой при комнатной температуре, обычно содержащие нетоксичные β-стабилизирующие элементы (Ta, Nb, Zr), обладающие низким модулем упругости и высокой биосовместимостью, перспективные для медицинских имплантатов.
Твёрдость материала, измеренная на нанометровом масштабе (часто методом индентирования), отражающая локальные механические свойства поверхностных слоёв, покрытий и наноструктурированных материалов.

Свойство материала не вызывать отторжения или токсических реакций в биологической среде; биоинертные покрытия (например, Ti-Ta) минимизируют воспалительные процессы и способствуют интеграции имплантата.

nodes.name: Apolar Collector
nodes.definition: Nonpolar hydrocarbon-based flotation reagent used to hydrophobize mineral surfaces by physical adsorption and wetting. The slice describes petroleum-derived apolar collectors such as kerosene, mineral oils, and heavy petroleum fractions.
nodes.text: Apolar Collector (аполярный собиратель, аполярные собиратели, неполярный собиратель)

nodes.name: Physical Adsorption
nodes.definition: Reversible sorption mechanism in which reagents bind to mineral or bubble surfaces through weak intermolecular interactions rather than electron transfer. In flotation, it produces a comparatively small heat effect and is easily removed by washing or dilution.

nodes.name: Van der Waals Forces
nodes.definition: Weak intermolecular forces that act between atoms and molecules without forming classical chemical bonds. In mineralogy and flotation, they are characteristic of apolar surfaces and contribute to low wettability and hydrophobic behavior.
nodes.text: Van der Waals Forces (силы Ван-дер-Ваальса, ван-дер-ваальсовы силы)

nodes.name: Polarizability
nodes.definition: Ability of a molecule or molecular fragment to form an induced dipole under an external electric field. In flotation, higher polarizability strengthens the attraction of apolar hydrocarbon collectors to ionically bonded mineral surfaces and improves fixation.
nodes.text: Polarizability (поляризуемость, способность к образованию мягкого диполя)

nodes.name: Viscosity
nodes.definition: Resistance of a fluid to flow, which reflects the intensity of intermolecular interactions and the molecular architecture of the hydrocarbon phase. In the slice, viscosity is used as a practical criterion for the hydrophobizing effectiveness and retention strength of apolar collectors on mineral surfaces.

nodes.name: Complanarity
nodes.definition: Geometric property in which all atoms of a molecular framework lie in one plane. For aromatic hydrocarbons, complanarity contributes to more stable adsorption and stronger fixation on mineral surfaces than in comparable aliphatic structures.

nodes.name: Induction Interaction
nodes.definition: Component of intermolecular attraction in which a permanent dipole induces a dipole in a neighboring molecule or surface fragment. It is one of the contributions to weak adsorption forces relevant to flotation systems.

nodes.name: Dipole Moment
nodes.definition: Measure of charge separation in a molecule or molecular fragment. In water, high dipole moments strengthen intermolecular interactions and contribute to liquid association and structuring.
nodes.text: Dipole Moment (дипольный момент, значительный дипольный момент)

nodes.name: Work of Adhesion
nodes.definition: Energy per unit area required to separate two contacting phases at an interface, such as a liquid and a mineral surface. In flotation, it is a key indicator of how strongly water or an apolar reagent can bind to a mineral surface.

nodes.name: Adhesion
nodes.definition: Attractive interaction between two different phases at their interface, such as water and a mineral surface. Adhesion governs liquid spreading, bubble attachment, and the strength of reagent fixation on mineral particles.

nodes.name: Selective Attachment to Air Bubbles
nodes.definition: Mechanism by which certain mineral particles preferentially adhere to injected air bubbles and are transported to the surface. This selectivity enables separation of minerals from suspension.
nodes.text: Selective Attachment to Air Bubbles (избирательное прилипание к пузырькам воздуха)

nodes.name: Mineral Beneficiation
nodes.definition: Industrial processing area focused on separating valuable minerals from gangue and improving the quality of mined raw materials. Flotation is one of the key methods used in this application.

nodes.name: Flotation Machine
nodes.definition: An apparatus in which pulp aeration, selective mineralization of bubbles, froth formation, froth retention, and froth discharge are carried out. Flotation machines are designed to maximize recovery and selectivity while minimizing energy use.

nodes.name: Main Flotation
nodes.definition: The first flotation operation in a scheme, used to separate a target group of minerals from the feed. In polymetallic flowsheets, several main flotations may be used sequentially for different valuable components.

nodes.name: Control Flotation
nodes.definition: A flotation operation applied to tailings or tail-branch products to recover residual floatable mineral and reduce losses to tailings. It serves as a cleanup step after primary flotation.
nodes.text: Control Flotation (контрольная флотация, очистная флотация, контрольные флотации)

nodes.name: Recleaning Flotation
nodes.definition: A repeat flotation operation applied to primary concentrates or concentrate-branch products to raise concentrate grade. It removes entrained gangue and improves the quality of the final concentrate.
nodes.text: Recleaning Flotation (перечистная флотация, перечистка, перечистные флотации)

nodes.name: Automated Process Control System
nodes.definition: An industrial control system used to monitor, regulate, and optimize flotation-plant operations through centralized continuous measurement, local automatic control loops, and automated decision logic. In the slice, it is described as the basis for stable process control, measurement processing, and control of technological units and mechanisms.
nodes.text: Automated Process Control System (АСУТП, автоматизированная система управления технологическими процессами)

nodes.name: Sodium Cyanide
nodes.definition: An inorganic cyanide reagent used in flotation as a depressant and complexing agent. In the slice, it binds dissolved copper ions, lowers their concentration in solution, and thereby promotes desorption of copper xanthate from mineral surfaces.

nodes.name: Sodium Sulfide
nodes.definition: An inorganic sulfide depressant used in flotation. The slice describes it as a reagent that suppresses many sulfide minerals and sulfidized oxidized minerals by introducing sulfide and hydrosulfide species into the pulp.

nodes.name: Separate Storage of Toxic Reagents
nodes.definition: An operational and safety requirement that toxic flotation reagents be stored separately in dedicated rooms and handled separately during crushing, dissolution, and dosing. The slice highlights this as a strict safety rule for cyanides and sodium sulfide in flotation plants.
nodes.text: Separate Storage of Toxic Reagents (раздельное хранение ядовитых реагентов, специализированное хранение цианидов и сернистого натрия)
aliases: специализированное хранение цианидов и сернистого натрия

nodes.name: Coal
nodes.definition: Carbonaceous sedimentary material that can exhibit high natural hydrophobicity and respond well to apolar collectors. In the slice, coal is cited among minerals/materials that can be floated by hydrophobic surface interactions.

nodes.name: Graphite
nodes.definition: Low-polarity carbonaceous mineral used as an example of a hydrophobic surface in flotation theory. It is not readily wetted by water and therefore behaves differently from silicate minerals.

nodes.name: Native Sulfur
nodes.definition: Naturally occurring elemental sulfur present in ore bodies as a recoverable mineral commodity. It is the principal feed material in sulfur ore beneficiation and is processed by gravity, flotation, thermal, and extraction routes.
nodes.text: Native Sulfur (самородная сера, элементарная сера природного происхождения)

nodes.name: Talc
nodes.definition: Hydrophobic magnesium silicate mineral commonly removed from ores by flotation. The slice notes separation of talc from mica as a practical cationic-collector application.

nodes.name: Hydrophobicity
nodes.definition: Tendency of a surface or particle to resist wetting by water and preferentially interact with a gas phase. In flotation, higher hydrophobicity promotes bubble attachment and froth recovery.

nodes.name: Flotation Recovery
nodes.definition: Process KPI expressing the fraction of valuable mineral transferred into the froth concentrate. In the slice, recovery is used to compare the effect of individual collectors and their combinations on galena flotation.

nodes.name: Frother Reagent
nodes.definition: Reagent class that stabilizes bubble size and froth structure in flotation pulp. Frothers improve bubble dispersion, froth persistence, and the selectivity of particle recovery.

nodes.name: Slime Coating
nodes.definition: Formation of a fine-slime layer on a larger mineral particle surface. Such coatings block direct bubble attachment, increase hydrophilicity, and suppress flotation of the underlying mineral.
nodes.text: Slime Coating (шламовые покрытия, шламовая пленка, наличие шламового покрова)

nodes.name: Droplet Fixation
nodes.definition: A flotation mechanism in which apolar collector droplets attach to the surface of floatable particles rather than acting only through dissolved species. In coal flotation, it is described as the main mode of action of apolar collectors.
nodes.text: Droplet Fixation (капельное закрепление, капельное прилипание, droplet attachment)

nodes.name: Emulsification of Apolar Reagents
nodes.definition: Dispersion of apolar flotation reagents into fine droplets in the pulp, often assisted by surface-active substances. In the slice, emulsification improves the distribution and collecting action of oils and other apolar reagents in coal flotation.
nodes.text: Emulsification of Apolar Reagents (эмульгирование аполярных реагентов, эмульгирование масел)

nodes.name: Coal Beneficiation
nodes.definition: Industrial processing domain focused on upgrading coal by removing mineral matter and improving fuel quality. It includes gravity separation, flotation, briquetting, and thermal treatment routes mentioned in the study guide.
nodes.text: Coal Beneficiation (обогащение угля, технология обогащения угля)

nodes.name: Coal Flotation
nodes.definition: Flotation application used for coal cleaning and recovery of carbonaceous material. The slice identifies several low-cost frothers and byproduct reagents as suitable for coal flotation.

nodes.name: Graphite Flotation
nodes.definition: Mineral beneficiation application aimed at recovering graphite from flake, dense-crystalline, and cryptocrystalline ores. The process relies on graphite's natural hydrophobicity and is strongly affected by surface oxidation, impurities, and the presence of fine liberated flakes.

nodes.name: Native Sulfur Flotation
nodes.definition: Beneficiation application for recovering native sulfur from sulfur-bearing ores. The process is used to produce sulfur concentrate for downstream autoclave melting, while rejecting gangue and minimizing contamination by slimes and carbonate minerals.
nodes.text: Native Sulfur Flotation (флотация самородной серы, флотация серных руд)

nodes.name: Talc Flotation
nodes.definition: Beneficiation application for separating talc from associated magnesite, chlorite, chromite, and oxidized talc-containing feeds. It exploits talc's high natural hydrophobicity and often requires combined frother and apolar collector action.
nodes.text: Talc Flotation (флотация талька, флотационное обогащение талькомагнезитового камня)

nodes.name: Coal Flotation Technology (1972)
nodes.definition: A bibliographic source on coal flotation technology, cited as a practical reference for coal beneficiation circuits, frothers, and apolar collectors.
nodes.text: Coal Flotation Technology (1972) (Пиккат-Ордынский А. А., Острый В. А. Технология флотационного обогащения углей. М., Недра, 1972, Технология флотационного обогащения углей)
aliases: Пиккат-Ордынский А. А., Острый В. А. Технология флотационного обогащения углей. М., Недра, 1972

nodes.name: Gases and Reagents on Minerals in Flotation (1950)
nodes.definition: A bibliographic source on the interaction of gases and reagents with minerals in flotation, cited as an early theoretical foundation for interfacial effects.
nodes.text: Gases and Reagents on Minerals in Flotation (1950) (Плаксин И. П. Воздействие газов и реагентов на минералы во флотационном процессе. 1950, Воздействие газов и реагентов на минералы во флотационном процессе)
aliases: Плаксин И. П. Воздействие газов и реагентов на минералы во флотационном процессе. 1950
Воздействие газов и реагентов на минералы во флотационном процессе

nodes.name: Alkaline Medium
nodes.definition: An alkaline pulp condition required for safe and effective cyanide use in flotation. The slice states that free alkali shifts cyanide hydrolysis to the left, suppressing HCN release and improving reagent efficiency.

nodes.name: Hydraulic Trap
nodes.definition: A compact gravity concentrator used in milling-classifier circuits to recover free gold and associated heavy minerals with low water demand. It is typically built as an inverted pyramid or cone, where coarse particles are retained near the inlet or on a screen while finer material settles into the chamber for discharge as concentrate.

nodes.name: Jigging Machine
nodes.definition: A device for gravity concentration that creates a pulsating liquid flow through a particle bed to stratify material by density. In the slice, it is used for gold and platinum-bearing feeds over a broad particle-size range.

nodes.name: Sluice
nodes.definition: An inclined gravity-concentration device in which slurry flows as a thin film over a channel with riffles, traps, or a soft lining. Heavy particles settle and are retained near the bottom while lighter gangue is carried away, making the unit suitable for gold-bearing sands and fine placer material.

nodes.name: Activated Carbon
nodes.definition: Porous carbon adsorbent added to flotation pulp to capture dissolved gold from solution and reduce metal losses. In cyanide-based lead-zinc flotation, it is used to suppress gold dissolution losses and can then report to the lead concentrate.
nodes.text: Activated Carbon (активированные угли, активированный древесный уголь, активированный уголь, древесный активированный уголь, порошкообразный древесный активированный уголь)

nodes.name: Copper Sulfate
nodes.definition: Copper sulfate species formed during oxidation of copper sulfides in pulp. It is part of the secondary chemistry that modifies sulfide surfaces and can influence subsequent flotation behavior.
nodes.text: Copper Sulfate (сульфат меди, CuSO4, медный купорос)

nodes.name: Potassium Dichromate
nodes.definition: An inorganic oxidizing salt used in flotation as a suppressing regulator for sulfide minerals. In the slice, it is cited as a treatment that increases hydrophilicity of galena surfaces and prevents stable bubble attachment.
nodes.text: Potassium Dichromate (бихромат калия, дихромат калия, K2Cr2O7)

nodes.name: Sodium Sulfite
nodes.definition: An inorganic reducing/suppressing reagent used in sulfide flotation. In the slice, it is noted to have a suppressing action similar to cyanide-related reagents, although with somewhat poorer technological results.

nodes.name: Zinc Sulfate
nodes.definition: An inorganic zinc salt used in flotation as a suppressing reagent, especially for zinc sulfide minerals. In the slice, it is used together with cyanide to intensify depression of sphalerite and reduce cyanide consumption.
nodes.text: Zinc Sulfate (цинковый купорос, сульфат цинка, ZnSO4)

nodes.name: Collective Flotation
nodes.definition: A flotation scheme in which several valuable components are recovered together into a single bulk concentrate. It is used when joint recovery is easier than immediate separation of individual minerals.

nodes.name: Collective-Selective Flotation
nodes.definition: A scheme in which several valuable minerals are first recovered together as a bulk concentrate and then separated from each other after additional conditioning or regrinding. It is especially useful for finely intergrown ores.

nodes.name: Dichromate Depression
nodes.definition: A selective flotation regime in which chromate or dichromate reagents are used to suppress galena and other lead-bearing sulfides. It is applied when lead is the dominant valuable component and the objective is to prevent lead from reporting to the froth.
nodes.text: Dichromate Depression (хромпиковый метод, метод подавления хромпиком, дихроматный метод подавления)

nodes.name: Gravity Concentration
nodes.definition: Physical beneficiation method based on density differences between mineral particles. In the slice, it is used ahead of flotation to recover coarse gold particles and reduce the load on subsequent flotation circuits.
nodes.text: Gravity Concentration (гравитационное обогащение, гравитационные методы обогащения)

nodes.name: Hellstrand Method
nodes.definition: Selective flotation method for lead-zinc ores based on depression of zinc sulfide with sodium sulfide. It is a narrower special-case route than cyanide-based schemes and is applied only to certain ore compositions.

nodes.name: Konev-Debrina Desorption Method
nodes.definition: Selective separation route for collective sulfide concentrates in which sodium sulfide is used to desorb collectors from mineral surfaces before Pb-Zn separation. The desorbed collector is removed from the process together with the desorbent by filtration, decantation, or thickening.
nodes.text: Konev-Debrina Desorption Method (метод А. С. Конева и Л. Б. Дебриной, метод десорбции собирателя сернистым натром)
aliases: метод А. С. Конева и Л. Б. Дебриной

nodes.name: Pallanch Method
nodes.definition: Selective lead-zinc flotation method that uses sodium sulfite, sodium thiosulfate, or sulfur dioxide together with zinc sulfate to depress sphalerite. It avoids cyanide-based drawbacks, but its applicability is more limited across ore types.

nodes.name: Sheridan-Griswold Method
nodes.definition: Classic selective flotation scheme for lead-zinc ores in which sphalerite is depressed with cyanide, or cyanide plus zinc sulfate, in alkaline medium. Lead is floated first; the suppressed ZnS is then activated with copper sulfate and floated in a second stage.

nodes.name: Beneficiation Cost Per Ton
nodes.definition: Economic KPI describing the total cost of processing one ton of ore, including reagents, energy, labor, depreciation, and related operating expenses. The slice uses this metric to compare flotation plants and shows that higher throughput lowers unit cost.
nodes.text: Beneficiation Cost Per Ton (стоимость обогащения 1 т руды, удельная себестоимость, себестоимость обогащения)

nodes.name: Gold Recovery
nodes.definition: The fraction of gold transferred from the ore feed into the pregnant solution or final product during leaching and recovery operations. In the slice, it is used to compare heap, tank percolation, and agitated cyanidation, where poor classification and clays reduce recovery while fine grinding and aeration improve it.
nodes.text: Gold Recovery (извлечение золота, степень извлечения золота, gold extraction)

nodes.name: Selectivity
nodes.definition: The degree to which a collector or surface process acts preferentially on one mineral phase over others. In the slice, selectivity is governed by the solidophilic group and by the specificity and strength of surface bonding.

nodes.name: Noble Metal Flotation
nodes.definition: Mineral beneficiation domain focused on recovering gold, silver, and platinum-group metals from ores and placers. In the slice, it is used as a processing route both for direct noble-metal recovery and for preconcentration before cyanidation or smelting.
nodes.text: Noble Metal Flotation (флотация благородных металлов, флотация noble metals)

nodes.name: Copper-Molybdenum Ore Flotation
nodes.definition: Specialized flotation application for copper-molybdenum ores. The slice notes that the OP-SCB frother reagent is useful in some copper-molybdenum flotation circuits.
nodes.text: Copper-Molybdenum Ore Flotation (флотация медно-молибденовых руд, флотация медно-молибденовой руды)

nodes.name: Polymetallic Ore Flotation
nodes.definition: Flotation process used to recover multiple valuable minerals from complex polymetallic feeds. The text refers to this application when discussing combined frothers, selective frothers, and collector–frother interactions.
nodes.text: Polymetallic Ore Flotation (флотация полиметаллических руд, коллективная флотация полиметаллических руд)

nodes.name: Copper-Zinc Ore Flotation
nodes.definition: Selective flotation route for copper-zinc polymetallic ores. In the slice, cyanide-based and cyanide-free suppressing regimes are discussed for improving separation of copper minerals from zinc sulfides.
nodes.text: Copper-Zinc Ore Flotation (флотация медно-цинковых руд, флотация медно-цинковой руды)

nodes.name: Copper-Nickel Ore Flotation
nodes.definition: A beneficiation domain focused on separating copper and nickel sulfide minerals, typically chalcopyrite, pentlandite, and pyrrhotite. The process often combines collective flotation, staged selection, magnetic separation, and reagent schemes tailored to differences in oxidation and activation behavior.
nodes.text: Copper-Nickel Ore Flotation (флотация медно-никелевых руд, флотация медно-никелевой руды)

nodes.name: Sulfide Molybdenum Ore Flotation
nodes.definition: Flotation application for sulfide molybdenum ores containing molybdenite together with other sulfides. The slice notes that sodium sulfide can depress the accompanying sulfides while leaving molybdenite recoverable.
nodes.text: Sulfide Molybdenum Ore Flotation (флотация сульфидных молибденовых руд, флотация молибденовых руд)

nodes.name: Bismuth Ore Flotation
nodes.definition: A beneficiation application focused on selective recovery of bismuthinite, native bismuth, and related bismuth sulfides. The slice describes it as a sulfide flotation problem with subsequent acid leaching and cementation when concentrate quality is insufficient.
nodes.text: Bismuth Ore Flotation (флотация висмутовых руд, обогащение висмутовых руд флотацией)

nodes.name: Antimony Ore Flotation
nodes.definition: A beneficiation application for stibnite-bearing ores. The slice notes activation by heavy-metal salts, depression by cyanides, and selective separation from mercury sulfide and other sulfides.
nodes.text: Antimony Ore Flotation (флотация сурьмяных руд, обогащение сурьмяных руд флотацией)

nodes.name: Mercury Ore Flotation
nodes.definition: A beneficiation application for cinnabar-bearing ores and related mercury-containing products. The slice emphasizes the strong sensitivity of mercury recovery to oxidation state, oxygen concentration, and depressant addition.
nodes.text: Mercury Ore Flotation (флотация ртутных руд, обогащение ртутных руд флотацией)

nodes.name: Oxidized and Mixed Nonferrous Ore Flotation
nodes.definition: A flotation application covering oxidized and mixed copper, lead, and zinc ores. The slice presents sulfidization followed by sulfhydryl-collector flotation as the principal route for these hard-to-float feeds.
nodes.text: Oxidized and Mixed Nonferrous Ore Flotation (флотация окисленных и смешанных руд цветных металлов, флотация окисленных минералов цветных металлов)
aliases: флотация окисленных и смешанных руд цветных металлов

nodes.name: Fluorite Ore Flotation
nodes.definition: A flotation application focused on recovering fluorite from ores containing calcite, quartz, barite, or other carbonate and silicate gangue. It usually relies on selective depression of gangue minerals and carefully chosen anionic collectors.
nodes.text: Fluorite Ore Flotation (флотация флюоритовых руд, обогащение флюоритовых руд флотацией)

nodes.name: Phosphorite Flotation
nodes.definition: A beneficiation application for phosphorite ores in which phosphate-bearing material is separated from quartz, carbonates, glauconite, and other gangue minerals. The text describes both direct anionic flotation and reverse cationic flotation routes, including staged schemes for carbonatized feeds.
nodes.text: Phosphorite Flotation (флотация фосфоритов, обогащение фосфоритов флотацией)

nodes.name: Technico-Economic Indicators of Flotation
nodes.definition: A set of production and economic indicators used to evaluate flotation processes and plant performance. Typical components include unit beneficiation cost, energy consumption, water consumption, throughput, and labor productivity, which together determine process efficiency and operating cost.
nodes.text: Technico-Economic Indicators of Flotation (технико-экономические показатели флотации, технико-экономические показатели)

nodes.name: Particle Size
nodes.definition: Characteristic linear size of ore particles after crushing or grinding. In the slice, particle size controls permeability, percolation rate, and gold liberation: coarse porous ore can be heap-leached, while finer grinding accelerates cyanidation in agitated systems.
nodes.text: Particle Size (крупность, размер частиц, grain size)

nodes.name: Degree of Liberation
nodes.definition: Fraction of mineral grains that are freed from intergrowths after comminution. It is a key determinant of flotation separability because insufficient liberation leaves composite particles that respond ambiguously to reagents.
nodes.text: Degree of Liberation (степень раскрытия, раскрытие минералов, степень раскрытия минералов)

nodes.name: Pulp Density
nodes.definition: Mass concentration of the solid phase in a flotation pulp. It controls viscosity, mixing intensity requirements, and the effectiveness of reagent contact with mineral surfaces.
nodes.text: Pulp Density (плотность пульпы, содержание твердого в пульпе)

nodes.name: Elevated Pulp Temperature
nodes.definition: A heated flotation-pulp regime used to improve handling of long-chain carboxylic collectors that are solid or poorly dispersible at room temperature. In the slice, temperatures around 40–60 °C or higher are recommended for such reagents to enable dosing and flotation performance.
nodes.text: Elevated Pulp Temperature (повышенная температура пульпы, нагрев пульпы, 40–60 °C)

nodes.name: Full Water Recycle
nodes.definition: An operating constraint requiring that process waters be cleaned and returned to circulation instead of being discharged. In flotation it reduces fresh-water demand, but it also forces the process regime to tolerate dissolved salts and other recycled-water impurities.
nodes.text: Full Water Recycle (полный водооборот, полное оборотное водоснабжение, полное использование оборотных вод)

nodes.name: Noble Metals
nodes.definition: A group of chemically stable metals with high resistance to oxidation and other chemical attack. In the slice, this group includes gold, silver, platinum, and the platinum-group metals.

nodes.name: Gold
nodes.definition: A precious metal mentioned in the context of cyanide flotation suppression. Cyanides can dissolve gold and thereby lower gold recovery into the froth product, which is an important practical limitation.

nodes.name: Silver
nodes.definition: Native metal included in the classification of flotation feed materials. It is relevant as an example of a naturally occurring metal phase that may occur with sulfides and other ore constituents.

nodes.name: Platinum
nodes.definition: Native metal included among naturally occurring metals in flotation classification. It is relevant as a noble metal phase associated with complex ore assemblages.

nodes.name: Palladium
nodes.definition: A platinum-group noble metal listed among the platinoids in the slice. It is characterized by high chemical resistance and very low natural abundance.

nodes.name: Ruthenium
nodes.definition: A platinum-group noble metal listed among the platinoids in the slice. It is a rare, chemically stable metal with very low natural abundance.

nodes.name: Rhodium
nodes.definition: A platinum-group noble metal listed among the platinoids in the slice. It is part of the rare noble-metal set distinguished by high chemical stability and scarcity.

nodes.name: Osmium
nodes.definition: A platinum-group noble metal listed among the platinoids in the slice. It is one of the rarest noble metals and is noted in the text as highly chemically stable.

nodes.name: Iridium
nodes.definition: A platinum-group noble metal listed among the platinoids in the slice. It belongs to the highly chemically resistant metals used to define the noble-metals group.

nodes.name: Chemical Stability
nodes.definition: Resistance of a metal to chemical interaction with surrounding media, especially oxidation and formation of oxygen compounds. The slice identifies this as a defining property of noble metals.

nodes.name: Natural Abundance
nodes.definition: Concentration of an element in natural materials or the Earth's crust. The slice gives very low mass fractions for noble metals, linking their scarcity to high economic value.
nodes.text: Natural Abundance (распространенность в природе, содержание в природе, массовая доля в земной коре)

nodes.name: Romanteev 2007
nodes.definition: Bibliographic source for the учебное пособие on precious-metals metallurgy published by MИСиС in 2007. It provides the theoretical and technological framework for extraction, processing, and refining of noble metals.
nodes.text: Romanteev 2007 (Романтеев Ю.П. Металлургия благородных металлов, Металлургия благородных металлов: Учебное пособие)

nodes.name: Precious Metal Metallurgy
nodes.definition: Industrial and academic field focused on extraction, beneficiation, hydrometallurgy, pyrometallurgy, and refining of noble metals such as gold, silver, platinum, and platinoids. In the slice, it is presented as the subject of the textbook and includes processing of ores and intermediate products.
nodes.text: Precious Metal Metallurgy (металлургия благородных металлов, металлургия драгоценных металлов)

nodes.name: Placer Ore
nodes.definition: Secondary ore material formed by weathering and redistribution of primary deposits, where liberated gold particles are concentrated in sediments. Placer ores are usually easier and cheaper to mine and can contain free gold with relatively low cutoff grades.
nodes.text: Placer Ore (россыпная руда, россыпные руды, золотосодержащие россыпи)

nodes.name: Primary Gold Ore
nodes.definition: Gold-bearing ore hosted in bedrock formations, typically in veins and primary rock masses. It commonly contains gold together with sulfides, quartz, and other gangue minerals, and is a major feed for gravity, flotation, and cyanidation routes.
nodes.text: Primary Gold Ore (коренная золотая руда, золотые руды коренного типа, жильная золотая руда)

nodes.name: Kerargyrite
nodes.definition: Silver chloride mineral occurring mainly in oxidized silver ores. It is relatively easy to recover by cyanidation and amalgamation because of its high reactivity compared with refractory silver sulfosalts.
nodes.text: Kerargyrite (кераргирит, роговое серебро, horn silver, AgCl)

nodes.name: Argentite
nodes.definition: Silver sulfide mineral mentioned as a secondary surface phase in ore alteration. It is relevant to flotation because its formation on other sulfides can modify surface chemistry and hydrophobicity.

nodes.name: Stephanite
nodes.definition: Silver-antimony sulfosalt mineral forming refractory silver ore bodies. It is less amenable to direct cyanidation than simple silver sulfides and commonly requires more intensive pretreatment.

nodes.name: Pyrargyrite
nodes.definition: Silver-antimony sulfosalt mineral of refractory silver ores. Its complex sulfosalt structure makes direct cyanidation difficult, so it is usually considered in specialized silver beneficiation schemes.

nodes.name: Proustite
nodes.definition: Silver-arsenic sulfosalt mineral occurring in significant silver deposits. It is a refractory silver phase whose extraction is more difficult than that of silver chloride or argentite.

nodes.name: Discrasite
nodes.definition: Silver-antimony mineral belonging to the class of refractory silver-bearing sulfosalts. It can form substantial ore bodies but is difficult to extract by direct cyanidation.

nodes.name: Polybasite
nodes.definition: Complex silver-copper sulfosalt mineral. It is a refractory silver-bearing phase that does not undergo direct cyanidation without pretreatment such as roasting.

nodes.name: Tetrahedrite
nodes.definition: Copper-silver antimony sulfosalt mineral occurring in polymetallic silver ores. Like polybasite, it is generally refractory to direct cyanidation and is processed with specialized pretreatments.

nodes.name: Argentojarosite
nodes.definition: Secondary silver-bearing iron sulfate mineral typical of oxidized ores and iron-cap zones. It is difficult to recover by flotation and becomes amenable to cyanidation only after chlorinating roast pretreatment.

nodes.name: Amalgamation
nodes.definition: Historical extraction method in which gold, silver, or platinum is selectively dissolved into mercury to form an amalgam. After washing, squeezing, and mercury distillation, a crude precious-metal product is obtained and the mercury is regenerated.

nodes.name: Cyanidation
nodes.definition: Hydrometallurgical extraction method that dissolves gold and some associated noble-metal species with cyanide solutions. The slice describes flotation as being combined with cyanidation either before or after flotation, and also notes that cyanidation can remove cyanide-sensitive gold-bearing fractions from ore.

nodes.name: Flotation
nodes.definition: Physico-chemical separation method in which fine particles selectively attach to gas bubbles and rise to the froth layer. In beneficiation, it exploits differences in surface properties of minerals.

nodes.name: Oxidative Roasting
nodes.definition: High-temperature pretreatment in an oxidizing atmosphere used to decompose refractory sulfide minerals before cyanidation. In the slice, it is applied to arsenopyrite-bearing ores to remove arsenic as volatile trioxide and improve downstream gold extraction.
nodes.text: Oxidative Roasting (окислительный обжиг, окислительный обжиг руд, oxidizing roast)

nodes.name: Autoclave Oxidation
nodes.definition: Pressure oxidation pretreatment used to decompose sulfide minerals before further precious-metal recovery. It is applied when fine or submicroscopic gold is locked in sulfides and must be liberated before cyanidation.
nodes.text: Autoclave Oxidation (автоклавное окисление, автоклавное окислительное разложение)

nodes.name: Chlorinating Roasting
nodes.definition: Thermal pretreatment in a chlorine-bearing atmosphere used to transform refractory silver-bearing minerals into forms more amenable to downstream extraction. In the slice, it is required before cyanidation of argentojarosite-containing ores.

nodes.name: Silver Recovery
nodes.definition: Process KPI representing the fraction of silver transferred from the feed into the leachate or final recovered product. In the reported study it is used alongside gold recovery to compare direct cyanidation with the roasting–cyanidation route.

nodes.name: Economic Gold Cutoff Grade
nodes.definition: Minimum gold content required for profitable mining and processing under a given deposit and technology regime. The threshold depends strongly on ore type, mining method, and recovery cost, and is much lower for placers than for many primary gold ores.
nodes.text: Economic Gold Cutoff Grade (рентабельный минимум содержания золота, экономический бортовой сорт, cutoff grade for gold ore)

nodes.name: Free Gold
nodes.definition: Gold present as liberated metallic grains rather than locked in other minerals. It is the most readily recoverable gold form and is typically amenable to gravity concentration and standard cyanidation when not coated by passivating films.

nodes.name: Sulfide Mineral
nodes.definition: Mineral class whose surfaces are often naturally amenable to oil wetting and collector adsorption. Sulfide minerals are central feedstocks for early oil flotation and later froth flotation processes.
nodes.text: Sulfide Mineral (сульфидные минералы, сульфиды, сульфидная руда)

nodes.name: Shaking Table
nodes.definition: A gravity separation apparatus with an inclined, riffled deck that oscillates to separate particles by density and size. Heavy grains migrate to the concentrate side, while lighter particles are washed to tailings by the water flow.

nodes.name: Soft-Lined Sluice
nodes.definition: A sluice-type gravity concentrator with a compliant lining that promotes retention of heavy particles during flow. It is used for coarse gold recovery where selective trapping of dense grains is required.
nodes.text: Soft-Lined Sluice (шлюз с мягким покрытием, шлюзовая драга)

nodes.name: Drum Concentrator
nodes.definition: A rotating gravity concentration device that separates heavy and light particles using centrifugal and hydrodynamic effects inside a drum. In the slice, it is listed among wet gravity apparatus for gold and platinum recovery.
nodes.text: Drum Concentrator (барабанный концентратор, барабанный гравитационный концентратор)

nodes.name: Short-Cone Hydrocyclone
nodes.definition: A hydrocyclone with a short conical section used in wet gravity separation to classify and concentrate dense particles. The reduced cone length intensifies centrifugal stratification and makes the unit suitable for fine heavy-mineral recovery.
nodes.text: Short-Cone Hydrocyclone (короткоконусный гидроциклон, гидроциклон короткоконусного типа)

nodes.name: Density
nodes.definition: Mass per unit volume of a material. The slice uses density to distinguish the heavy and light platinum-metal subgroups and to compare noble metals as a family of very dense materials.

nodes.name: Settling Velocity
nodes.definition: The rate at which a particle moves downward through a liquid under gravity or an imposed flow field. In gravity concentration, differences in settling velocity between dense and light minerals are the basis of stratification and separation.
nodes.text: Settling Velocity (скорость оседания, скорость падения частиц)

nodes.name: Belt Sluice
nodes.definition: A continuous sluice in which a moving rubber belt with a rough or ribbed surface carries the slurry counter-current to the belt motion. It provides continuous concentrate removal, higher throughput than stationary sluices, and is used mainly for concentrate cleanup and some sulfide ores.
nodes.text: Belt Sluice (ленточный шлюз, непрерывный шлюз на резиновой ленте)

nodes.name: Vibrational Sluice
nodes.definition: A sluice equipped with vibration on the deck to improve particle stratification and wash-off of accumulated concentrate. Vibration increases separation efficiency for gold-bearing ores compared with a stationary sluice, especially when fine heavy particles must be retained on the deck.
nodes.text: Vibrational Sluice (вибрационный шлюз, вибрационный шлюз для промывки золотосодержащих руд)
aliases: вибрационный шлюз для промывки золотосодержащих руд

nodes.name: Particle Classification
nodes.definition: Separation of ground material into size fractions during comminution circuits. In flotation preparation, classification is used to remove fine slimes and return coarse fractions to grinding for better liberation control.
nodes.text: Particle Classification (классификация, предварительная классификация, контрольная классификация)

nodes.name: Concentrate Yield
nodes.definition: The mass fraction of final concentrate obtained from the feed in a beneficiation or flotation circuit. It is a core process KPI because it determines product quantity, influences concentrate grade, and is used together with recovery to evaluate flowsheet performance.
nodes.text: Concentrate Yield (выход концентрата, yield of concentrate, mass yield of concentrate)

nodes.name: Quartz
nodes.definition: Highly polar silicate mineral used as an example of a hydrophilic surface. Water readily spreads on quartz because of the relatively small polarity mismatch.

nodes.name: Water
nodes.definition: Strongly polar liquid phase that serves as the continuous medium in flotation suspensions. Its interaction with mineral surfaces largely determines wetting behavior and separation selectivity.

nodes.name: Mercury
nodes.definition: The elemental metallic phase of mercury, noted in the slice as recoverable by flotation from metallurgical products. Its flotation behavior is similar to native gold and depends strongly on pulp chemistry and oxygen content.

nodes.name: Calcium Hydroxide
nodes.definition: An alkaline reagent widely used in flotation as a low-cost pH regulator and pyrite depressant. It is commonly dosed as milk of lime, and its use shifts pulp chemistry toward conditions that suppress pyrite flotation and alter surface hydration.
nodes.text: Calcium Hydroxide (известь, известковое молоко, Ca(OH)2, lime)

nodes.name: Copper Hydroxide
nodes.definition: Hydroxide precipitate formed from dissolved copper after lime addition. In amalgamation practice, it removes copper from the pulp and helps prevent copper contamination of mercury, improving the quality of the amalgam.

nodes.name: Gold Amalgam
nodes.definition: Product of gold amalgamation consisting of mercury with dissolved gold and dispersed solid phases. It may contain gold in solution, gold–mercury intermetallic compounds, and residual solid particles, and can become brittle when contaminated with copper or iron.

nodes.name: Mineral Oil
nodes.definition: Nonpolar organic liquid used as the wetting phase in oil flotation. It selectively wets sulfide particles, promotes agglomeration, and helps them rise to the pulp surface.

nodes.name: Mercury Non-Coalescence
nodes.definition: Formation of stable, non-coalescing mercury droplets under the influence of oils, carbonaceous matter, graphite, and mechanical agitation. It reduces mercury wetting of gold, increases mercury losses with tailings, and is harmful to amalgamation efficiency.
nodes.text: Mercury Non-Coalescence (пемзование ртути, образование устойчивых некоалесцирующих капель ртути)

nodes.name: Overgrinding
nodes.definition: Excessive comminution that produces too many ultrafine particles and slimes, often after the ore has already reached adequate liberation. It reduces flotation selectivity, increases reagent consumption, and complicates downstream solid-liquid separation.

nodes.name: Fine Particle Size
nodes.definition: Particle-size regime in which surface phenomena dominate the behavior of solids in suspension. Flotation is especially effective for these fine particles, typically below about tenths of a millimeter.
nodes.text: Fine Particle Size (малые размеры частиц, частицы размером в десятые доли миллиметра)
aliases: частицы размером в десятые доли миллиметра

nodes.name: Internal Amalgamation
nodes.definition: Amalgamation carried out simultaneously with grinding inside the milling apparatus. It allows freshly exposed gold surfaces to contact mercury immediately, before they become coated with sulfides, gangue, or oxidation films.

nodes.name: External Amalgamation
nodes.definition: Amalgamation performed outside the grinding device, usually on sluices or in dedicated amalgamators. It processes already ground material and is more sensitive to surface contamination of gold particles than internal amalgamation.

nodes.name: Runner Mill
nodes.definition: Heavy grinding mill with rotating runners that crush and abrade ore on a hardened bed. In the slice, it is used for internal amalgamation so that mercury contacts gold during comminution.

nodes.name: Amalgamation Barrel
nodes.definition: Small rotating cylindrical apparatus used for internal amalgamation of rich concentrates or small batches. It combines mixing, limited grinding, and mercury contact in a closed drum.

nodes.name: Amalgamation Sluice
nodes.definition: Inclined sluice lined with amalgamated copper sheets for external amalgamation. Pulp flows over the mercury-bearing surface, where gold particles wet and adhere to the amalgam layer.

nodes.name: Wettability
nodes.definition: Ability of a liquid to spread on and adhere to a solid surface. In flotation, wettability depends strongly on the polarity mismatch between the liquid and the mineral surface.

nodes.name: Mercury Diffusion into Gold
nodes.definition: Diffusion-controlled penetration of mercury into gold during the second stage of amalgamation. This process leads to gold–mercury solid solutions and intermetallic phases that determine the final structure and brittleness of the amalgam.
nodes.text: Mercury Diffusion into Gold (диффузия ртути в золото)

nodes.name: Potassium Cyanide
nodes.definition: An inorganic cyanide depressant and complexing reagent used in flotation. It acts similarly to sodium cyanide by binding dissolved copper ions and shifting surface equilibrium away from collector fixation.

nodes.name: Calcium Cyanide
nodes.definition: A cyanide reagent used for gold leaching as a cheaper alternative to sodium cyanide. The slice notes that it is often supplied as a fused salt mixture (cyanplav) and typically requires a higher consumption rate than NaCN for comparable cyanidation performance.

nodes.name: Oxygen
nodes.definition: Diatomic gas formed during water electrolysis and used as a bubble-forming phase in electroflotation. It can be used together with or separately from hydrogen to influence flotation behavior.

nodes.name: Pyrite
nodes.definition: Iron sulfide mineral used as an example of a sulfide phase whose flotation properties can change after interaction with copper sulfate. It is relevant to sulfide activation and surface oxidation chemistry.

nodes.name: Marcasite
nodes.definition: Iron sulfide mineral discussed as one of the sulfides whose flotation response is altered by copper sulfate treatment. Its surface chemistry can be modified to change hydrophobicity and collector interaction.

nodes.name: Pyrrhotite
nodes.definition: Iron sulfide mineral that oxidizes rapidly in flotation pulp and often occurs together with copper sulfides and pyrite in sulfide ores. Its surface state is highly sensitive to dissolved oxygen and pH, which strongly affects collector response and separation behavior.

nodes.name: Tellurium
nodes.definition: A chalcogen impurity in silver anodes and silver-gold alloys that strongly disrupts electrorefining. It can form difficult-to-handle tellurium compounds, produce gray spongy deposits at low electrolyte concentrations, and must be removed before refining.

nodes.name: Sulfur
nodes.definition: A nonmetallic element used in the text as an example of a crystal whose cleavage exposes weak intermolecular interactions. Its surface properties help illustrate why some minerals are naturally hydrophobic.

nodes.name: Sodium Hydroxide
nodes.definition: Strong alkali used to raise pulp pH in flotation circuits. The slice notes that increasing pH with sodium hydroxide strongly suppresses gold flotation, reflecting the sensitivity of surface chemistry and collector fixation to alkalinity.
nodes.text: Sodium Hydroxide (едкий натр, каустическая сода, NaOH)

nodes.name: Calcium Carbonate
nodes.definition: Insoluble carbonate precipitate formed when sodium carbonate is added to lime-containing cyanide solutions. It is used to remove calcium hardness before aluminum cementation and to prevent formation of insoluble calcium aluminates.
nodes.text: Calcium Carbonate (карбонат кальция, CaCO3, осадок карбоната кальция)

nodes.name: Gypsum
nodes.definition: A soluble calcium sulfate mineral present in ores and coal that can affect foaming behavior in flotation pulps. Its dissolved ions contribute to electrolyte effects on bubble stabilization and froth formation.

nodes.name: Cyanide Complexation
nodes.definition: Formation of highly stable metal-cyanide complexes in solution, which lowers the activity of dissolved metal ions and drives further dissolution of the metal surface. In the slice, this mechanism is central to gold and silver cyanidation through formation of dicyano complexes.
nodes.text: Cyanide Complexation (комплексообразование цианидом, образование цианидных комплексов, связывание катионов Au+ и Ag+ цианидом)
aliases: связывание катионов Au+ и Ag+ цианидом

nodes.name: Cyanide Hydrolysis
nodes.definition: Acid-base transformation in aqueous pulp where cyanide ions are converted into hydrocyanic acid and hydroxide is generated. This shifts cyanide speciation with pH and reduces the concentration of flotation-active CN- at lower pH values.
nodes.text: Cyanide Hydrolysis (гидролиз цианидов, гидролиз цианистого натрия)

nodes.name: Cyanide Concentration
nodes.definition: Process-condition parameter describing the free cyanide content in cyanidation liquors. In the slice, it has an optimum range because too little cyanide slows gold dissolution, while excess cyanide increases reagent loss and can suppress overall extraction by intensifying side reactions.
nodes.text: Cyanide Concentration (концентрация цианида, содержание цианида в растворе, концентрация NaCN)

nodes.name: pH
nodes.definition: Acidity/alkalinity parameter of the aqueous pulp. In the slice, sulfide oxidation forms acidic species and lowers pulp pH, which in turn changes mineral surface chemistry and flotation response.

nodes.name: Cyanide Consumption
nodes.definition: Operational KPI describing the amount of cyanide consumed per unit ore or precipitate processed. It is driven by dissolution losses, complex formation, and solution regeneration efficiency, and directly determines the cost of cyanidation circuits.
nodes.text: Cyanide Consumption (расход цианида, удельный расход цианида, потери цианида)

nodes.name: Reagent Consumption
nodes.definition: Operational KPI describing the amount of flotation reagent required per unit of ore or concentrate. Lower reagent consumption is one of the main economic advantages of using collector combinations in flotation practice.
nodes.text: Reagent Consumption (расход реагента, расход собирателя, удельный расход собирателя)

nodes.name: HCN Emission
nodes.definition: Volatile release of hydrocyanic acid from acidified cyanide liquors or tailings ponds. It creates an acute air-pollution and occupational-safety hazard and is one of the main reasons cyanide effluents must be neutralized before storage or disposal.
nodes.text: HCN Emission (выделение синильной кислоты, испарение HCN, выделение HCN)

nodes.name: Ferrous Sulfate
nodes.definition: An iron(II) sulfate reagent used in flotation as a depressant or conditioning additive. In the slice, it is combined with sulfite ions to suppress galena, including copper-activated galena, during selective lead separation.
nodes.text: Ferrous Sulfate (железный купорос, сульфат железа(II), FeSO4)

nodes.name: Ferric Sulfate
nodes.definition: Inorganic iron(III) sulfate formed during sulfide oxidation in aqueous systems. It acts as an aggressive oxidizing medium that accelerates sulfide-to-sulfate conversion and generates acidity that changes mineral surface chemistry.
nodes.text: Ferric Sulfate (сульфат железа(III), Fe2(SO4)3, сернокислое железо(III))

nodes.name: Basic Iron Sulfate
nodes.definition: A sparingly soluble ferric hydroxy-sulfate phase formed during hydrolysis of ferric sulfate in wet oxidizing conditions. It is an intermediate product in sulfide oxidation and can subsequently transform into ferric hydroxide, contributing to cyanide consumption and pulp contamination.
nodes.text: Basic Iron Sulfate (основной сульфат железа(III), Fe2O3·SO3, основной сульфат окисного железа)

nodes.name: Sulfuric Acid
nodes.definition: Strong mineral acid used in flotation-related processing to acidify pulp and generate carbon dioxide bubbles in the Potter-Delprat process. It can also alter surface chemistry and mineral liberation behavior.

nodes.name: Cyanide Ion
nodes.definition: The anionic form of cyanide present in alkaline solution. In flotation pulp it complexes copper ions, and its speciation is strongly controlled by pH because it is converted to hydrocyanic acid in acidic media.

nodes.name: Thiocyanate Ion
nodes.definition: A sulfur–carbon–nitrogen anion formed in cyanide solutions during oxidation of sulfides and reaction of cyanide with elemental sulfur. Its formation consumes cyanide, but the slice notes that lead treatment can rapidly convert more harmful sulfide species into thiocyanate.

nodes.name: Thiosulfate Ion
nodes.definition: Soluble sulfur oxyanion formed during oxidation of sulfide minerals in aqueous pulp. Its presence indicates partial sulfide oxidation and accompanies changes in pulp chemistry that can alter flotation behavior.

nodes.name: Sulfate Ion
nodes.definition: An inorganic oxyanion formed during oxidation of sulfide minerals. In flotation systems, sulfate-ion formation is associated with surface oxidation, dissolution of oxidized species, and changes in surface hydration and collector adsorption behavior.

nodes.name: Sulfite Ion
nodes.definition: An inorganic oxyanion used in flotation reagent systems as a reducing and depressing species. In the slice, sulfite ions are paired with ferrous sulfate to suppress galena and improve lead–copper selectivity.

nodes.name: Sulfide Ion
nodes.definition: A divalent sulfur anion present in sulfide-reagent solutions and pulp. In the slice, it acts as a potential-determining ion for sulfide minerals and helps displace collector ions from the surface.

nodes.name: Ferrous Cyanide
nodes.definition: An insoluble iron(II) cyanide precipitate that forms when ferrous hydroxide reacts with cyanide in alkaline solution. In cyanidation circuits, it represents a transient iron-cyanide phase that can further dissolve in excess cyanide to form ferrocyanide.

nodes.name: Ferrocyanide Ion
nodes.definition: A hexacyanoferrate(II) complex anion formed in alkaline cyanide solutions when iron(II)-bearing species react with excess cyanide. It is a key intermediate in the formation of blue iron-cyanide precipitates and reflects side chemistry that consumes cyanide in pulp.

nodes.name: Prussian Blue
nodes.definition: A deep-blue ferric hexacyanoferrate precipitate formed by oxidation of ferrocyanide or by direct reaction between Fe3+ and ferrocyanide species. Its appearance in cyanide solutions indicates insufficient protective alkali and unwanted iron-cyanide side reactions.
nodes.text: Prussian Blue (берлинская лазурь, Fe4[Fe(CN)6]3, синяя окраска цианистых растворов)

nodes.name: Polysulfides
nodes.definition: A family of sulfur-rich anions formed during partial oxidation and rearrangement of sulfide species in cyanide pulp. Their presence indicates complex sulfide-side chemistry and contributes to nonproductive consumption of oxidants and cyanide.

nodes.name: Polythionates
nodes.definition: A family of sulfur oxyanions generated during oxidation of sulfide minerals in cyanide systems. They are part of the complex sulfur speciation in pulp and reflect advanced oxidation pathways beyond simple sulfate and thiosulfate formation.

nodes.name: Metallic Iron
nodes.definition: Sacrificial cementation metal used to precipitate dissolved precious metals from acid-treated cyanide liquors. It also removes small amounts of dissolved copper from precipitate slurries before final product upgrading.

nodes.name: Acidic Medium
nodes.definition: Flotation pulp condition with lowered pH. In the slice, acidic medium restores floatability of suppressed pyrite by removing iron hydroxide films and is used to modify sulfide surface chemistry during reactivation.

nodes.name: Surface Passivation by As/Sb Films
nodes.definition: Formation of dense, thin reaction films from arsenic- and antimony-bearing decomposition products on gold and silver surfaces. These films hinder solvent access, suppress dissolution kinetics, and reduce cyanidation recovery.
nodes.text: Surface Passivation by As/Sb Films (плотные тонкие пленки мышьяка и сурьмы, пассивирующие пленки As/Sb, surface film passivation)
aliases: плотные тонкие пленки мышьяка и сурьмы

nodes.name: Thickening
nodes.definition: Частичное обезвоживание пульпы, основанное на осаждении твердых частиц под действием разности плотностей между твердой и жидкой фазой. Обычно используется как предоперация перед фильтрацией и позволяет сократить объем перерабатываемой суспензии.

nodes.name: Leaching
nodes.definition: Hydrometallurgical dissolution process in which one or more components are selectively transferred from a solid feed into a liquid solvent. In the slice, leaching is the general framework for cyanide dissolution of noble metals and for diffusion-controlled mass transfer from finely ground ore particles.
nodes.text: Leaching (выщелачивание, растворение одного или нескольких компонентов из массы твердых частиц)
aliases: растворение одного или нескольких компонентов из массы твердых частиц

nodes.name: Decantation
nodes.definition: A solid-liquid separation step in which clarified solution is poured or drawn off from a settled pulp or slurry without full filtration. In cyanidation circuits it is used to recover gold-bearing solution after leaching and to reduce downstream solids loading.
nodes.text: Decantation (декантация, слив осветленного раствора, отделение раствора от осадка)

nodes.name: Filtration
nodes.definition: Solid-liquid separation method used to remove leach residue or concentrate solids from a pregnant solution or slurry. In hydrometallurgical flowsheets it is applied after leaching and before downstream metal recovery, and it directly affects solution clarity and metal losses.

nodes.name: Central Drive Thickener
nodes.definition: A pulp-thickening vessel with a central rotating rake mechanism that accelerates settling of suspended solids and withdraws clarified overflow. In cyanidation flowsheets it is used before leaching to reduce slurry volume, lower pumping and mixing demand, and improve process stability.
nodes.text: Central Drive Thickener (сгуститель с центральным приводом, центрально-приводной сгуститель, чан-сгуститель)

nodes.name: Leaching Tank
nodes.definition: An agitated vessel used to contact ore pulp with leaching reagents so that valuable components dissolve into the liquid phase. In the slice, such tanks are operated either periodically or as a cascade of continuously working units with mechanical, pneumatic, or pneumomechanical mixing.
nodes.text: Leaching Tank (чан для выщелачивания, агитатор для выщелачивания, чан выщелачивания)

nodes.name: Impeller
nodes.definition: Rotating aeration element in a flotation machine that disperses air into fine bubbles and creates local turbulence and pressure drops. It is central to bubble formation, cavitation, and mixing in the pulp.

nodes.name: Rotary Drum Vacuum Filter
nodes.definition: Continuous vacuum filter with a slowly rotating perforated drum segmented into cells and covered by filter cloth. Part of the drum is immersed in pulp, the cake forms on the outer surface, and the cake is removed by a scraper after filtration.
nodes.text: Rotary Drum Vacuum Filter (барабанный вакуум-фильтр, барабанный вакуумный фильтр)

nodes.name: Liquid-to-Solid Ratio
nodes.definition: Process parameter describing the volume of leach liquor relative to the mass of ore being treated. In heap leaching it is low compared with tank processing, and it strongly affects reagent concentration, percolation behavior, and overall throughput.
nodes.text: Liquid-to-Solid Ratio (отношение жидкого к твердому, Ж:Т, L/S ratio)

nodes.name: Diffusion-Controlled Dissolution
nodes.definition: Dissolution regime in which mass transfer through the thin saturated boundary layer around a particle is slower than the surface chemical reaction and therefore limits the overall rate. The slice describes this as the controlling mechanism for noble-metal leaching, with the diffusion layer acting as the main resistance to dissolution.
nodes.text: Diffusion-Controlled Dissolution (диффузионно-ограниченное растворение, диффузионная область реакции, ограничение скорости диффузией)

nodes.name: Boundary Layer Diffusion
nodes.definition: Mass-transfer mechanism by which reagents move through the thin liquid film adjacent to a mineral surface. In flotation conditioning, it governs how quickly reagents reach the surface and become fixed or desorbed.
nodes.text: Boundary Layer Diffusion (диффузия в пограничном слое, диффузия к поверхности минерала)

nodes.name: Surface Oxidation
nodes.definition: A degradation process in which dissolved oxygen reacts with a mineral surface, especially sulfide minerals, forming oxidized layers or species. This typically increases hydrophilicity and reduces flotation performance by weakening bubble attachment.

nodes.name: Specific Energy Consumption
nodes.definition: Electrical energy consumed per unit mass or volume of pulp processed. In flotation machine design, this KPI should be minimized to improve process economics and reduce operating cost.
nodes.text: Specific Energy Consumption (удельный расход электроэнергии, энергоемкость процесса)

nodes.name: Ionite
nodes.definition: Water-insoluble high-molecular ion-exchange material containing ionogenic groups and mobile counterions. It selectively captures ions from electrolyte solutions by reversible ion exchange and is widely used for noble-metal recovery.

nodes.name: Styrene
nodes.definition: A vinyl aromatic monomer used as a base component for many synthetic ion-exchange resins. In the slice it defines the polymer backbone of styrene-DVB ionites, which determines swelling and mechanical durability.

nodes.name: Divinylbenzene
nodes.definition: A crosslinking comonomer used in styrene-based ion-exchange resins. Its content controls the degree of network crosslinking, which in turn affects swelling, pore accessibility, and resin rigidity.

nodes.name: Dicyanoaurate(I) Ion
nodes.definition: Stable complex anion formed when Au+ is bound by two cyanide ions in cyanide leaching solutions. It is the dissolved gold species that represents the thermodynamic endpoint of gold cyanidation in alkaline media.
nodes.text: Dicyanoaurate(I) Ion ([Au(CN)2]-, дицианоаурит-ион, комплексный анион золота в цианиде)

nodes.name: Dicyanoargentate(I) Ion
nodes.definition: Stable complex anion formed by silver ion binding with cyanide in alkaline cyanidation solutions. The slice describes this species as the dissolved form of silver that is analogous to dicyanoaurate during silver leaching.
nodes.text: Dicyanoargentate(I) Ion ([Ag(CN)2]-, дицианоаргентат-ион, комплексный анион серебра в цианиде)

nodes.name: Tetracyanozincate Ion
nodes.definition: Stable zinc-cyanide complex anion present in spent or impurity-rich cyanide liquors. It can adsorb at metal surfaces, participate in double-layer screening, and contribute to cyanide solution fatigue.
nodes.text: Tetracyanozincate Ion ([Zn(CN)4]2-, тетрацианцинкат-ион, комплексный анион цинка в цианиде)

nodes.name: Copper Cyanide Complex
nodes.definition: Soluble copper–cyanide complex formed when metallic copper or copper minerals dissolve in cyanide pulp. Its accumulation causes major cyanide consumption and slows gold dissolution in copper-bearing ores.
nodes.text: Copper Cyanide Complex ([Cu(CN)3]2-, цианидный комплекс меди, complex cyanide species of copper)

nodes.name: Thiourea
nodes.definition: A sulfur-containing organic reagent used as an effective gold desorbent from saturated anion-exchange resins. In acidic sulfate or hydrochloric media it forms a stable cationic gold complex, enabling elution of gold and co-desorption of silver and copper.

nodes.name: Swelling Coefficient
nodes.definition: The ratio of the swollen resin specific volume to the air-dry specific volume. It is a key structural parameter for ion-exchange resins because it controls pore accessibility, diffusion paths, and exchange kinetics; higher crosslinking generally lowers swelling.
nodes.text: Swelling Coefficient (коэффициент набухания, набухание ионита, swelling ratio)

nodes.name: Exchange Capacity
nodes.definition: The amount of ions that can be taken up by a unit mass of ionite. In cyanide sorption circuits it determines resin loading with gold and competing impurities, and it is reduced in real solutions by competitive adsorption of cyanide complexes and background anions.
nodes.text: Exchange Capacity (обменная емкость, полная обменная емкость, равновесная обменная емкость, рабочая обменная емкость)

nodes.name: Crosslinking Degree
nodes.definition: The extent of polymer network crosslinking in a resin, typically controlled by divinylbenzene content in styrene-based ionites. Higher crosslinking improves mechanical stability but reduces swelling and can slow ion diffusion into the bead interior.
nodes.text: Crosslinking Degree (степень сшивки, сшивка смолы, content of DVB)

nodes.name: Ion Exchange
nodes.definition: Reversible exchange of ions between an electrolyte solution and ionogenic groups fixed in a solid phase. It is the basic mechanism of ionite-based recovery of gold, silver, and other dissolved species from process liquors.

nodes.name: Gel Diffusion
nodes.definition: Transport of ions through the internal gel phase of an ion-exchange bead. It becomes the dominant kinetic limitation after the external film resistance decreases and governs the slow approach to equilibrium in resin sorption.
nodes.text: Gel Diffusion (гелевая диффузия, диффузия в зерне ионита)

nodes.name: Film Diffusion
nodes.definition: Mass transfer through the liquid boundary film adjacent to the resin surface. In ion-exchange sorption, this is often the initial rate-limiting step before the process becomes controlled by diffusion inside the bead.
nodes.text: Film Diffusion (пленочная диффузия, диффузия через пленку раствора)

nodes.name: Sorption Cyanidation
nodes.definition: A combined hydrometallurgical route in which cyanide leaching and simultaneous adsorption of dissolved precious metals on a sorbent occur in the same agitated circuit. In the slice, it is used to recover gold and silver from the flotation concentrate and from the calcine after roasting.
nodes.text: Sorption Cyanidation (сорбционное цианирование, agitation sorption cyanidation, cyanidation in sorption mode)

nodes.name: Ionite Regeneration
nodes.definition: A regeneration procedure that removes adsorbed gold and impurities from a saturated ion-exchange resin and restores its sorption performance for reuse. In the slice it is implemented by dynamic desorption in a vertical column, minimizing fresh resin consumption.
nodes.text: Ionite Regeneration (регенерация ионита, восстановление сорбционных свойств смолы, regeneration of resin)

nodes.name: Acidic Thiourea Elution
nodes.definition: A resin-regeneration desorption step in which loaded ion-exchange material is treated with acidic thiourea solutions to strip gold, silver, and copper from the sorbent. In the slice, this operation alone is insufficient for full regeneration because many impurities remain only weakly desorbed.
nodes.text: Acidic Thiourea Elution (элюирование тиомочевиной, кислотное элюирование тиомочевиной, элюирование смолы кислыми растворами тиомочевины)

nodes.name: Sorption Column
nodes.definition: A packed column used for adsorption recovery of gold from dilute pregnant solutions on activated carbon or ion-exchange resin. Countercurrent operation and staged transfer of sorbent make it suitable for preconcentration of noble metals.
nodes.text: Sorption Column (сорбционная колонна, колонна сорбции, угольная колонна)

nodes.name: Activated Carbon Loss
nodes.definition: Operational KPI describing the mass of activated carbon lost from the sorption circuit, including losses as fine fractions during circulation and handling. In the slice, these losses are reported as a major drawback of carbon sorption because they directly increase reagent cost and reduce process stability.
nodes.text: Activated Carbon Loss (потери сорбента, потери активированного угля, loss of sorbent)

nodes.name: Sorption Leaching
nodes.definition: A combined hydrometallurgical route in which cyanide leaching of gold-bearing pulp and simultaneous sorption of dissolved gold by ion-exchange resin are carried out in the same circuit. The process eliminates the need for separate clarification and filtration after cyanidation and increases gold recovery by lowering dissolved-gold concentration in the pulp.
nodes.text: Sorption Leaching (сорбционное выщелачивание, сорбционное цианирование, выщелачивание с сорбцией)

nodes.name: Pachuca Tank
nodes.definition: Высокий цилиндрический чан с коническим днищем и центральным аэролифтом для пневматического перемешивания пульпы. Аппарат обеспечивает интенсивную аэрацию без движущихся частей и широко применяется в цианировании золота.
nodes.text: Pachuca Tank (пачук, чан с центральным аэролифтом, pachuk)

nodes.name: Airlift
nodes.definition: A gas-lift transport device that uses injected air to raise pulp or slurry through a vertical channel. In flotation machines, it is used to circulate pulp and assist bubble generation and particle transport in the working zone.

nodes.name: Separation Screen
nodes.definition: A mesh-based separation device used to retain resin granules while allowing fine ore particles and solution to pass through. In sorption leaching circuits it enables countercurrent transfer of resin between Pachuca tanks and prevents loss of sorbent into the pulp stream.
nodes.text: Separation Screen (разделительная сетка, грохот, сетчатый разделитель)

nodes.name: Ion-Exchange Resin
nodes.definition: A polymeric solid containing fixed ionic functional groups capable of selectively binding dissolved metal complexes from solution. In cyanide metallurgy, ion-exchange resins are used for sorption recovery of gold and silver from cyanide liquors.

nodes.name: Electroelution
nodes.definition: An electrochemical desorption method used to strip gold and silver from loaded ion-exchange resin in an electrolytic cell. In the slice, it is applied for resin regeneration and for transferring precious metals into a cathodic deposit suitable for remelting and refining.

nodes.name: Electrolyzer
nodes.definition: An electrochemical cell used to recover dissolved precious metals from thiourea solutions by cathodic deposition and anodic water oxidation. In the slice, the apparatus is operated under controlled current, mixing, and temperature to increase deposition rate and manage gas evolution.

nodes.name: Adsorption
nodes.definition: Interfacial accumulation of ions or molecules on a solid or liquid surface. In flotation, adsorption controls reagent attachment to minerals and strongly affects selectivity and recovery.

nodes.name: Hydrometallurgy
nodes.definition: Metal extraction and purification domain based on aqueous solutions and leachates. Ion flotation is used here to recover dilute metal ions from process streams.

nodes.name: Thiourea Leaching
nodes.definition: Gold dissolution in acidic thiourea solutions using ferric sulfate as oxidant. It is a non-cyanide leaching route whose rate depends on pH, thiourea concentration, and oxidant concentration.

nodes.name: Sodium Cyanide Solution
nodes.definition: Aqueous cyanide lixiviant used for heap leaching and ore preparation. In the slice it is applied both to wet ore during stacking and to re-leach old heaps for improved gold recovery.
nodes.text: Sodium Cyanide Solution (раствор цианистого натрия, цианистый натрий в растворе)

nodes.name: Clay
nodes.definition: Fine-grained hydrophilic aluminosilicate material commonly present as slime gangue in flotation pulps. Clays can adsorb collectors, form slime coatings, and suppress flotation of valuable minerals.

nodes.name: High Pulp Solids Content
nodes.definition: Состояние пульпы с высоким содержанием твердой фазы, пригодное для работы в пневматических агитаторах типа пачука. Такое условие повышает требования к перемешиванию, но позволяет эффективно перерабатывать плотные суспензии.
nodes.text: High Pulp Solids Content (содержание твердого 50–60 %, густая пульпа, высокая концентрация твердого)

nodes.name: Rotary Kiln
nodes.definition: A rotating thermal-processing furnace used for calcination and regeneration operations under controlled atmosphere. In the slice, it is used to heat activated carbon without air access to remove organic contaminants and restore its sorption performance.
nodes.text: Rotary Kiln (барабанная вращающаяся печь, вращающаяся печь, rotary furnace)

nodes.name: Thermal Regeneration of Activated Carbon
nodes.definition: A regeneration route in which spent activated carbon is calcined at about 600–800 °C for a short time in the absence of air to destroy organic fouling species and restore sorption capacity. In the slice, the regenerated carbon is cooled, screened, and returned to cyanide sorption service.
nodes.text: Thermal Regeneration of Activated Carbon (термическая регенерация угля, прокалка угля, высокотемпературная регенерация угля)

nodes.name: Activated Carbon Sorption
nodes.definition: A recovery method in which dissolved noble-metal cyanide complexes are adsorbed onto activated carbon from solution. The text presents it as an increasingly important alternative to zinc cementation in cyanide processing of gold and silver.
nodes.text: Activated Carbon Sorption (сорбция активными углями, сорбция на активированном угле, угольная сорбция)

nodes.name: Electrowinning
