nodes.definition: An electrochemical recovery method in which dissolved noble-metal complexes are deposited onto a cathode from solution. In the slice it is one of the routes used to recover gold and silver from eluates after sorption.

nodes.name: Specific Cathode Surface Area
nodes.definition: Electroactive cathode area per unit electrolyzer volume or mass of cathode material. In the slice, increasing this parameter is the main way to intensify gold electrowinning from thiourea regenerate because deposition is limited by mass transfer to the cathode.
nodes.text: Specific Cathode Surface Area (удельная поверхность катода, развитая поверхность катода, катодная удельная поверхность)

nodes.name: Borax
nodes.definition: A borate flux used during smelting of cyanide precipitates and gold-silver alloys. It lowers slag melting temperature and helps separate noble-metal bullion from oxide and silicate impurities.

nodes.name: Potassium Nitrate
nodes.definition: An oxidizing nitrate flux added during smelting of cathode precipitates to oxidize metallic iron from the cathode basis and improve melt cleanup. It supports formation of a cleaner gold-silver product before refining.
nodes.text: Potassium Nitrate (калиевая селитра, нитрат калия, KNO3)

nodes.name: Sodium Nitrate
nodes.definition: An oxidizing nitrate flux used together with or instead of potassium nitrate in smelting of cathodic precipitates. It oxidizes residual metallic iron and helps produce a cleaner bullion for subsequent refinement.
nodes.text: Sodium Nitrate (натриевая селитра, нитрат натрия, NaNO3)

nodes.name: Gold-Silver Alloy
nodes.definition: Intermediate bullion product obtained by smelting cyanide precipitates or concentrates. Its fineness depends on the composition of the feed and the quality of slag separation, and it is typically sent for subsequent refining.
nodes.text: Gold-Silver Alloy (золотосеребряный сплав, доре, dore metal)

nodes.name: Precious Metal Cementation Precipitate
nodes.definition: A precipitate formed when dissolved gold and silver are reduced from cyanide solution by zinc dust or other cementing metals. It typically contains gold together with copper, zinc, lead, selenium, and silver and is routed to further refining or doré production.
nodes.text: Precious Metal Cementation Precipitate (цементное золото, цементный осадок, cementation sludge)

nodes.name: Zinc
nodes.definition: A sacrificial metallic reducing agent used to cement gold and silver from cyanide solutions. In cementation circuits, zinc acts as the anodic phase that dissolves while noble metals are reduced and deposited on its surface.

nodes.name: Lead Sulfate
nodes.definition: A sparingly soluble lead salt that can form on galena surfaces during oxidative or chromate-related suppression. It contributes to hydrophilic surface films and creates conditions for further exchange with chromate ions.

nodes.name: Selenium
nodes.definition: A chalcogen impurity present in silver-gold anode materials and copper-electrolytic slimes. In the slice, selenium mostly reports to anode slime as silver selenate-like species and has relatively limited influence on the electrorefining process.

nodes.name: Tungsten
nodes.definition: Refractory transition metal used in the slice as an example of a surface that can strongly chemisorb oxygen. It serves to illustrate that chemisorbed surface species may be bound with energies comparable to the cohesion of the substrate.

nodes.name: Sulfuric Acid Leaching
nodes.definition: Hydrometallurgical treatment in which oxidized metal-bearing minerals are contacted with sulfuric acid to dissolve the target metal into solution. In the slice, it is used as the first stage of the Mostovich process before cementation and flotation.
nodes.text: Sulfuric Acid Leaching (сернокислотное выщелачивание, кислотное выщелачивание серной кислотой, H2SO4 leaching)

nodes.name: Lead-Lined Leaching Vat
nodes.definition: An acid-resistant vessel lined with sheet lead for sulfuric-acid treatment of cyanide precipitates and related leach operations. It is designed to withstand aggressive media and to handle gas evolution under agitation or air bubbling with exhaust ventilation.
nodes.text: Lead-Lined Leaching Vat (свинцованный чан, футерованный листовым свинцом чан, leaching vat)

nodes.name: Roasting
nodes.definition: A high-temperature pre-treatment used to modify mineral surface chemistry before flotation. In the text, roasting activates phosphate minerals and removes carbonates, improving selectivity in phosphorite beneficiation.

nodes.name: Chamber Resistance Furnace
nodes.definition: An electrically heated chamber furnace used for laboratory or pilot roasting of mineral charges. In the slice it is equipped with silicon-carbide heaters and used to roast flotation concentrate at controlled temperatures in the 650–750 °C range.
nodes.text: Chamber Resistance Furnace (камерная печь сопротивления, камeрная печь, resistance furnace)

nodes.name: Sodium Carbonate
nodes.definition: An alkaline inorganic reagent used together with sodium silicate to increase depressant selectivity in flotation. It raises pulp alkalinity and helps condition mineral surfaces before subsequent separation.

nodes.name: Fluorite
nodes.definition: Calcium fluoride mineral commonly recovered by flotation with cationic or other selective collectors. The slice mentions fluorite as a target mineral in separation schemes involving alkyl sulfate and other reagents.

nodes.name: Reverberatory Furnace
nodes.definition: A smelting furnace in which charge is melted on the hearth under reflected heat from the roof and flame path. In the slice, it is used for smelting acid-treated cyanide precipitates and producing a gold-silver alloy or intermediate lead bullion.
nodes.text: Reverberatory Furnace (отражательная печь, плавильная печь с подом, reverberatory hearth furnace)

nodes.name: Arsine
nodes.definition: A highly toxic gaseous hydride of arsenic released during acid treatment of arsenic-bearing cyanide precipitates. Its formation is a major safety hazard during leaching and requires closed vessels and strong ventilation.

nodes.name: Stibine
nodes.definition: A highly toxic gaseous hydride of antimony released during acid treatment of antimony-bearing cyanide precipitates. It is a dangerous byproduct of the hydrogen evolution occurring in acidic sludge leaching.

nodes.name: Acid Consumption
nodes.definition: Operational KPI describing the mass of acid required to process a unit mass of cyanide precipitate or sludge. In the slice, sulfuric acid consumption is a key cost and safety parameter because it controls impurity removal and the amount of toxic gas evolved.
nodes.text: Acid Consumption (расход кислоты, удельный расход кислоты, потребление кислоты)

nodes.name: Silver Chloride
nodes.definition: A sparingly soluble silver salt formed when residual silver is precipitated from spent electrolyte with sodium chloride. In the slice it is then reduced to metallic silver with zinc dust or iron powder.
nodes.text: Silver Chloride (хлористое серебро, AgCl, chloride silver)

nodes.name: Tetrachloroaurate Ion
nodes.definition: The dissolved gold species present in chloroauric-acid electrolytes. It is the electrorefining feed species that forms from gold dissolution at the anode and is subsequently reduced on the cathode.
nodes.text: Tetrachloroaurate Ion ([AuCl4]-, тетрахлороаурат-ион, комплексный анион золота)

nodes.name: Dichloroaurate(I) Ion
nodes.definition: Monovalent gold chloro-complex formed during anodic dissolution of gold in chloride electrolyte. It coexists with tetrachloroaurate and contributes to the non-ideal electrochemical behavior of gold electrorefining, including apparent current efficiencies above 100%.

nodes.name: Chloride Ion
nodes.definition: A major inorganic anion in natural waters and process liquors. Chloride contributes to ionic strength and solution composition, which can alter flotation behavior indirectly through changes in interfacial chemistry and reagent activity.

nodes.name: Hydrogen Ion
nodes.definition: A positively charged aqueous species noted in the slice as being adsorbed more strongly than alkali-metal ions. Hydrogen ions influence surface charging, acidity, and the adsorption behavior of mineral surfaces in electrolyte solutions.

nodes.name: Chlorine
nodes.definition: A strong oxidizing halogen gas used to chlorinate molten crude gold and convert base metals and silver into chlorides. In the process described, chlorine selectively reacts with less noble impurities before gold and platinum-group metals.

nodes.name: Lead Chloride
nodes.definition: Sparingly soluble lead salt that forms in chloride electrolytes when lead dissolves from gold anodes. Its precipitation can create passivating surface films on the anode and disrupt stable gold electrorefining.

nodes.name: Bismuth
nodes.definition: The elemental metallic phase of bismuth, mentioned in the slice as a flotation-recoverable component in bismuth-bearing ores. Its flotation response is close to that of bismuth sulfide minerals.

nodes.name: Palladium Chloride
nodes.definition: Chloride species of palladium formed in gold anode dissolution under chloride electrorefining conditions. It is an electrolyte impurity that can later contaminate the cathodic gold deposit if allowed to accumulate.

nodes.name: Standard Electrode Potential
nodes.definition: Electrochemical potential of a redox couple measured under standard conditions. The slice gives standard electrode potentials for gold, platinum, palladium, and silver as a quantitative measure of noble-metal chemical stability and electron affinity.
nodes.text: Standard Electrode Potential (электродный потенциал, стандартный электродный потенциал, E0)

nodes.name: Electrical Conductivity
nodes.definition: Ability of water or pulp to conduct electric current through dissolved ions. The slice notes that purified distilled water has very low conductivity, while dissolved salts increase conductivity.

nodes.name: Electrolytic Refining
nodes.definition: An electrochemical refining route in which a precious-metal alloy is dissolved anodically and purified metal is deposited cathodically from solution. In the slice, it is presented as the most advanced route for high-purity gold and silver production.
nodes.text: Electrolytic Refining (электролитическое рафинирование, электролиз, электролитический аффинаж)

nodes.name: Wohlwill Process
nodes.definition: Electrolytic refining route for gold in chloride media that uses an asymmetric alternating-current component to prevent passivation of the anode by silver chloride. The process enables selective dissolution of gold and high-purity cathodic deposition while limiting chlorine evolution and anode crust formation.
nodes.text: Wohlwill Process (процесс Вольвилля, вольвиллевский процесс, asymmetric current gold electrorefining)

nodes.name: Hearth Roasting
nodes.definition: Oxidative roasting of sulfide concentrates on a hearth with mechanical or manual material movement. The method requires careful control of particle temperature to avoid calcine overheating, partial melting, and loss of porosity needed for subsequent cyanidation.
nodes.text: Hearth Roasting (подовый обжиг, обжиг на поду)

nodes.name: Two-Stage Roasting
nodes.definition: A roasting scheme in which the first stage is carried out with limited air access to volatilize arsenic as As2O3, and the second stage uses excess oxygen to oxidize sulfur. This sequence produces a more porous calcine with lower residual arsenic and sulfur, improving downstream cyanidation.

nodes.name: Oxidative-Chlorinating Roasting
nodes.definition: A high-temperature pretreatment in which sulfide concentrates are roasted with added sodium chloride in an oxidizing atmosphere. Chlorine is generated in situ from sulfur oxides and chloride, which helps open refractory gold-bearing mineral grains and improves subsequent cyanidation.
nodes.text: Oxidative-Chlorinating Roasting (окислительно-хлорирующий обжиг, хлорирующий окислительный обжиг)

nodes.name: Calcine Cyanidation
nodes.definition: Cyanide leaching of a roasted calcine product to recover precious metals after thermal pretreatment. In the reported process it follows arsenatizing roasting and is used to exploit the increased chemical accessibility of gold and silver in the roasted material.
nodes.text: Calcine Cyanidation (цианирование огарка, cyanidation of calcine, roast-calcine cyanidation)

nodes.name: Multi-Hearth Furnace
nodes.definition: A vertical roasting furnace with multiple stacked hearths and a central shaft carrying rabble mechanisms. It enables staged contact between concentrate and gas phase, improving control of roasting temperature, oxygen access, and product porosity compared with older single-hearth furnaces.

nodes.name: Fluidized Bed Roasting Furnace
nodes.definition: A roasting furnace in which the charge is intensely mixed in a fluidized state by the gas stream. Strong heat exchange prevents local overheating and calcine fusion, making the process more stable than hearth roasting for sulfide concentrates.
nodes.text: Fluidized Bed Roasting Furnace (печь кипящего слоя, обжиговая печь кипящего слоя, fluidized-bed furnace)

nodes.name: Cyclone
nodes.definition: A gas-solid separation unit that removes entrained dust from roasting off-gases by centrifugal separation. In roasting flowsheets, cyclones serve as the first-stage dust collector before finer gas cleaning.

nodes.name: Electrostatic Precipitator
nodes.definition: A gas-cleaning device that removes fine particulate matter from flue gas using an electrostatic field. In fluidized-bed roasting circuits, it is used to capture dust that escapes cyclone separation, including condensates of toxic arsenic trioxide.

nodes.name: Bag Filter
nodes.definition: Cloth-based filtration unit used for fine solution clarification in auxiliary or small-capacity circuits. It removes suspended solids before zinc precipitation or other hydrometallurgical steps.
nodes.text: Bag Filter (мешочный фильтр, мешочный фильтр для растворов)

nodes.name: Gold-Arsenic Flotation Concentrate
nodes.definition: A sulfide flotation concentrate containing gold and elevated arsenic, typically refractory to direct cyanidation because gold is finely disseminated and associated with arsenic-bearing sulfides. Such concentrates usually require oxidative pretreatment before leaching.
nodes.text: Gold-Arsenic Flotation Concentrate (золотосодержащий мышьяковистый флотоконцентрат, мышьяковистый флотоконцентрат, refractory gold-arsenic flotation concentrate)

nodes.name: Calcine
nodes.definition: The solid product obtained after roasting ore or concentrate under oxidizing or chlorinating conditions. In this slice the calcine is a porous, partially agglomerated arsenatizing-roast product that is subsequently subjected to cyanidation to recover gold and silver.

nodes.name: Arsenic Trioxide
nodes.definition: Volatile arsenic oxide produced during oxidative roasting of arsenopyrite-bearing ores. Removal of arsenic as this phase is used to prepare refractory gold ores for cyanidation.
nodes.text: Arsenic Trioxide (мышьяковистый ангидрид, As2O3, триоксид мышьяка)

nodes.name: Sodium Chloride
nodes.definition: A common soluble salt mentioned as an impurity that influences foaming in flotation systems. Dissolved sodium chloride modifies electrolyte concentration and can alter hydration-layer structure and bubble stability.
nodes.text: Sodium Chloride (хлористый натрий, NaCl, поваренная соль)

nodes.name: Sulfur Dioxide
nodes.definition: Gaseous reagent used in some lead-zinc flotation schemes together with zinc sulfate to suppress sphalerite. It acts as a non-cyanide depressant option in selective flotation of zinc-bearing sulfides.

nodes.name: Copper Sulfide Ore
nodes.definition: Ore feed dominated by copper sulfide minerals such as chalcopyrite, chalcocite, bornite and covellite, often with pyrite as an associated phase. In the slice, these ores are treated as the main industrial copper feedstock whose flotation response depends strongly on oxidation state, liberation and slime content.
nodes.text: Copper Sulfide Ore (медные сульфидные руды, сульфидные медные руды)

nodes.name: Anode Slime
nodes.definition: Insoluble residue formed during silver anode dissolution, enriched in gold, platinum-group metals, selenium, tellurium, and some hydrolized base-metal compounds. It is the main sink for noble impurities during electrorefining and a key intermediate for precious-metal recovery.
nodes.text: Anode Slime (анодный шлам, шлам, анодные шламы)

nodes.name: Hematite
nodes.definition: Iron oxide mineral commonly recovered by reverse or direct flotation routes. The slice lists hematite among minerals effectively floated by cationic collectors.

nodes.name: Arsenic Content
nodes.definition: Mass fraction of arsenic in ore, concentrate, or calcine. Elevated arsenic content is a key indicator of refractory behavior because it is associated with sulfide encapsulation, higher roasting demand, and reduced direct cyanidation response.

nodes.name: Ore Porosity
nodes.definition: The fraction of void space in broken ore that governs permeability to leach solutions. In heap leaching, higher porosity improves percolation, capillary penetration, and access of cyanide solution to gold-bearing surfaces.
nodes.text: Ore Porosity (пористость руды, пористость кусков руды)

nodes.name: Calcine Sintering
nodes.definition: A roasting failure mode in which excessive temperature causes partial melting or densification of the calcine. The resulting low-porosity product is poorly permeable to cyanide solutions, which reduces gold liberation and extraction efficiency.
nodes.text: Calcine Sintering (спекание огарка, оплавление огарка, плотный малопористый огарок)

nodes.name: Gold Surface Passivation by Low-Melting Films
nodes.definition: A roasting-induced failure mode in which molten or near-molten reaction products coat gold particles and block access of cyanide solutions. This passivation increases gold losses to cyanidation tailings because the metal becomes chemically inaccessible.
nodes.text: Gold Surface Passivation by Low-Melting Films (пленки легкоплавких соединений на поверхности золота, пассивирование золота пленками, поверхностные пленки легкоплавких соединений)
aliases: пленки легкоплавких соединений на поверхности золота

nodes.name: Heap Leaching
nodes.definition: Percolation leaching of crushed ore stacked on an impermeable pad and irrigated from above with a lixiviant, typically cyanide solution in gold processing. The method is widely used for low-grade ores because it is simple, low-cost, and suitable for large tonnages with slow solution percolation.
nodes.text: Heap Leaching (кучное выщелачивание, кучное выщелачивание золота)

nodes.name: Heap Detoxification
nodes.definition: Post-leaching treatment of a heap to destroy residual cyanide and other toxic reagents before ore removal or further handling. The slice describes oxidation-based detoxification using chlorine, hydrogen peroxide, permanganate, and related oxidants.
nodes.text: Heap Detoxification (детоксикация кучи, обезвреживание кучи, post-leach detoxification)

nodes.name: Heap Channeling
nodes.definition: Nonuniform flow of leach solution through preferential paths in a heap. It reduces contact with ore, worsens extraction uniformity, and is promoted by poor stacking, segregation, and fines migration.

nodes.name: Clay Compaction
nodes.definition: Loss of heap permeability caused by clay-rich material being compressed during stacking or equipment traffic. In the slice, this is a key reason for reduced gold recovery from clayey and high-carbonate ores and motivates lower heap heights.
nodes.text: Clay Compaction (уплотнение глинистых руд, уплотнение глинистой фракции)

nodes.name: Heap Leach Cycle Time
nodes.definition: Process KPI describing the time required to complete a heap leach campaign. The slice reports very different cycle times for accelerated and long-term leaching and shows that pelletization and ore preparation can shorten the cycle substantially.
nodes.text: Heap Leach Cycle Time (цикл выщелачивания, длительность цикла выщелачивания)

nodes.name: Cementation
nodes.definition: A hydrometallurgical recovery method in which dissolved metal is precipitated from solution by a more active reducing phase. In the slice it is used after hydrochloric-acid leaching to recover bismuth from solution.

nodes.name: Hot Cyanide Elution
nodes.definition: Regeneration/desorption method in which loaded activated carbon is treated with a hot alkaline cyanide solution to strip adsorbed gold and silver complexes. In the slice, it is described as the standard industrial elution route for carbon sorption circuits, operating typically at elevated temperature to accelerate desorption.
nodes.text: Hot Cyanide Elution (горячее цианистое элюирование, элюирование горячим цианистым раствором, desorption with hot cyanide solution)

nodes.name: Autoclave Desorption
nodes.definition: A high-temperature, high-pressure desorption route used to strip gold and silver from loaded activated carbon. It shortens elution time and reduces reagent consumption compared with atmospheric cyanide-alkali desorption.
nodes.text: Autoclave Desorption (автоклавная десорбция, десорбция под давлением, pressure desorption)

nodes.name: Activated Carbon Acid Wash
nodes.definition: Regeneration step in which activated carbon is treated with dilute nitric or hydrochloric acid to remove calcium carbonate deposits and part of the residual organic fouling. In the slice, acid washing is used to restore sorption activity before the carbon is returned to service.
nodes.text: Activated Carbon Acid Wash (кислотная промывка угля, кислотная обработка активированного угля, обработка разбавленной азотной или соляной кислотой)
aliases: обработка разбавленной азотной или соляной кислотой

nodes.name: Zinc Dust
nodes.definition: Finely divided zinc used as the cementing reagent for precipitation of gold and silver from cyanide solutions. Its high specific surface area increases cementation rate, and it is often lead-activated before use to reduce passivation and improve contact with solution.

nodes.name: Lead Nitrate
nodes.definition: A heavy-metal salt used for activation of stibnite before sulfhydryl-collector flotation. In the slice it belongs to the class of heavy-metal activators that improve antimony mineral recovery.
nodes.text: Lead Nitrate (азотнокислый свинец, нитрат свинца, Pb(NO3)2)

nodes.name: Aluminum Powder
nodes.definition: Finely divided aluminum used as a cementing agent for precious metals from cyanide solutions. It is slower than zinc because it wets poorly, but it oxidizes to aluminate species and regenerates cyanide during metal precipitation.
nodes.text: Aluminum Powder (алюминиевая пыль, алюминий в порошке, порошкообразный алюминий)

nodes.name: High-Carbon Ferromanganese
nodes.definition: Ferromanganese alloy used as a cementing reductant for recovering gold from thiourea solutions. In the slice, it is mentioned as an alternative to zinc or aluminum dust for metal precipitation from saturated thiourea regenerates.

nodes.name: Cementation Tank
nodes.definition: A vessel used to precipitate dissolved noble metals from solution by cementation, typically with zinc dust. In gold-recovery circuits it provides controlled mixing, solid-liquid contact, and settling of the cemented sludge before refining.
nodes.text: Cementation Tank (осадительный чан, осадительные чаны, осадительный чан с вакуум-рамами, cementation vat)

nodes.name: Vibrocementator
nodes.definition: A cementation apparatus in which vibration intensifies contact between zinc granules and metal-bearing solution. It is used to accelerate precipitation of gold and silver while improving reagent utilization and slurry transport.

nodes.name: Autoclave
nodes.definition: A sealed high-pressure reactor used for oxidative leaching of sulfide gold concentrates. It maintains elevated temperature and oxygen pressure so that sulfide minerals are decomposed while gold remains in the insoluble residue.

nodes.name: Low Arsenic Content
nodes.definition: A feed-solution condition under which zinc dust cementation remains effective. Elevated arsenic increases cementation difficulty and reagent loss, while low arsenic content allows cleaner precipitation of gold and silver.
nodes.text: Low Arsenic Content (низкое содержание мышьяка, малое содержание мышьяка)

nodes.name: Dissolved Oxygen Concentration
nodes.definition: Amount of oxygen dissolved in the flotation pulp liquid phase. It controls the rate of sulfide oxidation and can be intentionally raised by pre-aeration to improve selective separation of sulfides with different oxidation kinetics.
nodes.text: Dissolved Oxygen Concentration (концентрация растворенного кислорода, растворенный кислород, oxygen in pulp water)

nodes.name: Zinc Consumption
nodes.definition: Operational KPI describing the mass of zinc required to precipitate noble metals from cyanide solution. It is reduced by effective deaeration, solution clarification, and suppression of passivating side reactions.
nodes.text: Zinc Consumption (расход цинка, удельный расход цинка, потребление цинка)

nodes.name: Capital Expenditure
nodes.definition: Investment KPI describing the upfront cost of buildings, machinery, and plant infrastructure required to build flotation capacity. In the slice it is discussed per unit annual ore throughput and is one of the key economic measures of plant design.
nodes.text: Capital Expenditure (капитальные затраты, капитальные вложения, инвестиционные затраты)

nodes.name: Gold Loading on Activated Carbon
nodes.definition: The amount of adsorbed gold per unit mass of activated carbon. It controls when the sorbent is transferred to desorption, with the slice indicating working loadings of several kilograms of gold per ton of carbon before regeneration.
nodes.text: Gold Loading on Activated Carbon (насыщение угля золотом, загрузка золота на уголь, gold loading)

nodes.name: Specific Surface Area
nodes.definition: Surface area per unit mass of a particulate material. It increases as particle size decreases, making surface effects increasingly important in flotation.
nodes.text: Specific Surface Area (удельная поверхность, площадь поверхности на единицу массы)

nodes.name: Hydrochloric Acid
nodes.definition: A strong mineral acid used in hydrometallurgical treatment of bismuth-bearing flotation products. In the slice it is applied for leaching bismuth from low-grade concentrates before cementation.

nodes.name: Cathodic Current Density
nodes.definition: Electrorefining operating parameter describing current per unit cathode area. The text notes that lower current density is used when palladium is present in the anode metal to limit co-deposition and stabilize electrolyte composition.
nodes.text: Cathodic Current Density (плотность тока, катодная плотность тока, 300–400 А/м2)

nodes.name: Cathode Current Efficiency
nodes.definition: Process KPI expressing the fraction of electrical current that actually produces cathodic silver deposition. In the slice it is reduced by nitrate reduction, silver-copper co-deposition, and other parasitic reactions, so it directly controls energy efficiency and operating cost.
nodes.text: Cathode Current Efficiency (катодный выход по току, токовый выход, current efficiency)

nodes.name: Gold Hydrate
nodes.definition: A hydrated gold precipitate obtained from thiourea-regenerate solutions by alkaline treatment. It is a recoverable intermediate that is subsequently roasted or sent to electrolysis to obtain metallic gold.
nodes.text: Gold Hydrate (гидрат золота, осадок гидрата золота, гидратное золото)

nodes.name: Cyanide Toxicity
nodes.definition: A safety and environmental constraint associated with cyanide use in flotation. The slice emphasizes that cyanides require restricted handling because of their acute toxicity, release of HCN in acidic media, and impact on plant safety and reagent selection.
nodes.text: Cyanide Toxicity (токсичность цианидов, сильная токсичность цианидов)

nodes.name: Activated Carbon Attrition
nodes.definition: Mechanical degradation of activated carbon during transport, pumping, and cyclic column transfer, producing fine fractions that are lost with process streams. The slice identifies low mechanical strength and resulting sorbent losses as a key limitation of carbon sorption in cyanide circuits.
nodes.text: Activated Carbon Attrition (механическое разрушение угля, истирание угля, измельчение сорбента в мелкие фракции)

nodes.name: Iron Sulfide Treatment
nodes.definition: A cyanide-destruction method in which cyanides in free and dissolved form are decomposed by contact with iron sulfide. The process is carried out for 15–60 minutes and can be implemented by direct slurry addition or by percolation through an iron-sulfide bed.
nodes.text: Iron Sulfide Treatment (обработка сульфидом железа, разложение цианидов с помощью сульфида железа)
aliases: разложение цианидов с помощью сульфида железа

nodes.name: Iron Sulfide
nodes.definition: A precipitated iron sulfide reagent used to destroy free and dissolved cyanides in wastewater treatment. It is prepared by combining ferrous sulfate with a soluble sulfide and is applied either as a suspension or as a percolation bed.
nodes.text: Iron Sulfide (сульфид железа, FeS, осадок сульфида железа)

nodes.name: pH 7-8.5
nodes.definition: Operating pH window used for iron-sulfide cyanide treatment. In this range the added sulfide must exceed the total cyanide concentration by roughly a factor of three to achieve effective decomposition.

nodes.name: Residual Cyanide Concentration
nodes.definition: Process KPI describing the cyanide content remaining in treated wastewater or tailings liquor after detoxification. It is a direct measure of treatment completeness and environmental compliance, with lower values indicating more effective destruction or removal of cyanide species.
nodes.text: Residual Cyanide Concentration (остаточное содержание цианидов, остаточная концентрация цианид-ионов, концентрация цианидов после обезвреживания)

nodes.name: Ozonation
nodes.definition: Oxidative wastewater treatment using ozone generated from air or oxygen by electric discharge. In cyanide effluents it oxidizes cyanide and thiocyanate species, but it is comparatively expensive in both capital and energy costs.

nodes.name: Ozone
nodes.definition: Strong oxidizing gas used to convert trivalent arsenic into pentavalent arsenic before precipitation. In the slice, it is one of the oxidants applied for preparing wastewater for arsenate removal.

nodes.name: Cyanate Ion
nodes.definition: A much less toxic oxyanion formed during oxidative destruction of cyanide. In the slice it is the main product of SO2/air treatment and an intermediate species in subsequent oxidation to nitrogen and bicarbonate.

nodes.name: Maximum Permissible Concentration
nodes.definition: Regulatory limit on contaminant concentration in environmental media such as water bodies. In the slice, it is used for cyanide, thiocyanate, and arsenic species to define acceptable discharge levels for gold-plant wastewater.
nodes.text: Maximum Permissible Concentration (ПДК, предельно допустимая концентрация, maximum allowable concentration)

nodes.name: Chlorination
nodes.definition: Gold dissolution process using chlorine-bearing reagents to convert metallic gold into soluble chloro-complexes. In the slice, it is the classical pre-cyanide route used for polymetallic and slime-rich ores.

nodes.name: Prussian Blue Precipitation
nodes.definition: A cyanide-removal method based on converting CN- to ferrocyanide and precipitating ferric hexacyanoferrate(III) as Prussian blue. It can reduce cyanide to very low levels in synthetic solutions, but it is ineffective for industrial liquors with high thiocyanate content.
nodes.text: Prussian Blue Precipitation (осаждение берлинской лазури, метод берлинской лазури)

nodes.name: Bacterial Oxidation of Cyanides
nodes.definition: A two-stage biological treatment route for cyanide wastewater in which adapted microorganisms oxidize cyanide and thiocyanate, followed by nitrifying bacteria converting ammonia to nitrate. The method can reduce cyanide to near-zero levels under mild operating conditions.
nodes.text: Bacterial Oxidation of Cyanides (бактериальное окисление, биологическая обработка сточных вод)

nodes.name: Biological Contactor
nodes.definition: A rotating biological reactor used for cyanide wastewater treatment. In the slice it consists of a plastic housing with multiple driven discs that support biomass attachment and provide aeration and mixing during biological oxidation.
nodes.text: Biological Contactor (контактор, биологический контактор, вращающийся биоконтактор)

nodes.name: Phosphoric Acid
nodes.definition: A strong mineral acid used to create an acidic conditioning medium for staged flotation of carbonatized phosphorite ores. At sufficient dosage it promotes carbonate flotation first and is later replaced by alkaline conditions for phosphate mineral recovery.

nodes.name: Ferrous Chloride
nodes.definition: A soluble iron(II) chloride intermediate formed during chlorinating roasting when chlorine reacts with iron-bearing sulfides or oxides. It can further oxidize to ferric chloride, regenerating chlorine and sustaining the gas-phase chlorination cycle.

nodes.name: SO2/Air Oxidation
nodes.definition: An oxidative cyanide-destruction process in which a gas-air mixture containing sulfur dioxide is bubbled through wastewater in the presence of lime and a copper catalyst. Cyanide is converted mainly to cyanate, while thiocyanate removal is more selective than in chlorination or ozonation.
nodes.text: SO2/Air Oxidation (очистка стоков сернистым газом, процесс ИНКО, INCO process)

nodes.name: Air
nodes.definition: Gas phase used as bubble-forming medium in froth flotation. Air bubbles provide attachment sites for hydrophobic particles and are essential for efficient flotation separation.

nodes.name: Cyanide Oxidation Degree
nodes.definition: Process KPI describing the fraction of cyanide species converted to less toxic products during oxidation-based detoxification. In the INCO process described in the slice, the oxidation degree reaches about 99.9%.
nodes.text: Cyanide Oxidation Degree (степень окисления цианида, степень разложения цианидов)

nodes.name: SO2 Consumption
nodes.definition: Operational KPI expressing the mass of sulfur dioxide required per unit mass of cyanide treated. The slice reports an average demand of about 3.1 kg SO2 per 1 kg cyanide in the INCO cyanide-destruction process.
nodes.text: SO2 Consumption (расход сернистого газа, удельный расход SO2)

nodes.name: Lime Consumption
nodes.definition: Operational KPI describing the mass of lime required per unit mass of ore processed. In flotation practice it is a major cost and control parameter, with the text citing typical consumption on the order of 1.5–2 kg/t.
nodes.text: Lime Consumption (расход извести, удельный расход извести, расход известкового молока)

nodes.name: pH 9-10
nodes.definition: Operating pH range used for the SO2/air oxidation process. The mildly alkaline medium supports cyanide oxidation, enables lime control of acidity, and helps precipitate metals as hydroxides after treatment.
nodes.text: pH 9-10 (рН 9…10, слабощелочная среда для процесса ИНКО)

nodes.name: SO2 Utilization
nodes.definition: Process KPI describing the fraction of supplied sulfur dioxide that is effectively consumed in cyanide oxidation. The slice reports utilization of about 80% for the SO2/air detoxification route.
nodes.text: SO2 Utilization (степень использования сернистого газа, использование SO2)

nodes.name: Sodium Metabisulfite
nodes.definition: A sodium sulfite-derived reagent used as a carrier of sulfur dioxide in cyanide detoxification. It supplies both sulfite species and alkalinity for neutralization in SO2-based wastewater treatment.
nodes.text: Sodium Metabisulfite (метабисульфит натрия, пиросульфит натрия, Na2S2O5)

nodes.name: Mills-Crowe Acidification
nodes.definition: A cyanide-regeneration method in which cyanide solutions are acidified with sulfuric acid and the released hydrogen cyanide is captured in absorbers for recycle. The process can remove more than 90% of cyanide, but ferrocyanides and thiocyanates are not fully decomposed.
nodes.text: Mills-Crowe Acidification (подкисление, метод Миллс – Кроу, acidification of cyanide solutions)

nodes.name: Hydrocyanic Acid
nodes.definition: A weakly dissociated acid formed by hydrolysis/protonation of cyanide in water. In the slice, its formation at lower pH removes free cyanide ions from solution and deactivates the depressing action of cyanides.

nodes.name: Absorber
nodes.definition: Gas-scrubbing unit that contacts HCN-bearing air with an alkaline solution. It captures hydrocyanic acid as cyanide or sodium/potassium hydroxide solution and closes the regeneration loop.

nodes.name: pH 2.5-3
nodes.definition: Acidic operating window used in Mills-Crowe cyanide solution acidification. At this pH the target discharge concentration can be achieved within a few hours, but filtration before aeration may be required to avoid apparatus fouling by precipitates.
nodes.text: pH 2.5-3 (рН 2,5…3, кислая среда для подкисления растворов)

nodes.name: Electrochemical Cyanide Treatment
nodes.definition: Electrochemical destruction or transformation of cyanide compounds in wastewater, excluding ferrocyanides. The slice notes electrowinning of metal-cyanide complexes as one variant of this route.
nodes.text: Electrochemical Cyanide Treatment (электрохимическая обработка, электрохимическое разложение цианистых соединений)

nodes.name: State Educational Standard of Higher Professional Education
nodes.definition: Нормативное требование, задающее содержание, объём и результаты подготовки специалистов в высшей школе. В тексте выступает как регламентирующая рамка для построения учебной дисциплины и её самостоятельной работы.

nodes.name: Arsenatizing Roasting
nodes.definition: Thermochemical pretreatment in which arsenic-bearing sulfide concentrates are roasted below the melting point of gold-bearing components to convert refractory sulfides into more leachable calcine. The process improves gold accessibility by oxidizing arsenic and sulfur-bearing phases.
nodes.text: Arsenatizing Roasting (арсенатизирующий обжиг, окислительно-арсенатизирующий обжиг, oxidation arsenatizing roasting)

nodes.name: Cyanidation Resistance
nodes.definition: The tendency of an ore or concentrate to resist gold and silver dissolution in cyanide solution because the precious metals are finely disseminated or locked in sulfide/arsenic minerals. It is a practical descriptor of whether oxidative pretreatment is needed before leaching.
nodes.text: Cyanidation Resistance (упорность к цианистому процессу, cyanide resistance, refractoriness to cyanidation)

nodes.name: Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrometry
nodes.definition: Elemental analysis technique in which an argon plasma excites atoms and ions, and their emission lines are measured to determine composition. It is suitable for multi-element quantification in ores, concentrates, and calcines.
nodes.text: Inductively Coupled Plasma Optical Emission Spectrometry (оптико-эмиссионный анализ с индуктивно-связанной плазмой, ОЭС-ИСП, ICP-OES)

nodes.name: Atomic Absorption Spectrometry
nodes.definition: Analytical method that quantifies elements by measuring absorption of element-specific radiation by free atoms in the vapor phase. In the slice it is used for gold, silver, and general compositional analysis of sample and process products.
nodes.text: Atomic Absorption Spectrometry (атомно-абсорбционный анализ, AAS, атомная абсорбция)

nodes.name: X-ray Phase Analysis
nodes.definition: Diffraction-based method used to identify crystalline phases in ore, concentrate, and roast products. It reveals mineral transformations caused by roasting and is therefore useful for evaluating calcine formation and phase changes.

nodes.name: IR Spectroscopy
nodes.definition: Vibrational spectroscopic method used to identify functional groups and molecular bonding environments in solids or extracts. In the slice it supports chemical-state analysis of the concentrate and roasting products.

nodes.name: Gravimetric Analysis
nodes.definition: Classical quantitative analytical method based on measuring mass after selective precipitation, filtration, drying, or ignition. It is used to determine composition and mass fractions in mineral-processing samples.

nodes.name: Titrimetric Analysis
nodes.definition: Volumetric analytical method that determines analyte concentration from the amount of standard reagent consumed in a reaction. In ore-processing studies it is used for compositional and solution-chemistry measurements.

nodes.name: Photometric Analysis
nodes.definition: Analytical method that determines composition from the intensity of light absorption or transmission by a colored or derivatized sample. It is suitable for solution assays and compositional control in metallurgical experiments.

nodes.name: Fire Assay Atomic Absorption Analysis
nodes.definition: Combined precious-metal assay in which gold and silver are first concentrated by fire assay and then quantified by atomic absorption. It is a standard high-sensitivity method for determining noble-metal content in ores and concentrates.
nodes.text: Fire Assay Atomic Absorption Analysis (пробирный атомно-абсорбционный анализ, fire assay AAS)

nodes.name: Arsenopyrite
nodes.definition: Iron arsenic sulfide mineral commonly associated with gold in sulfide ores. The slice mentions it as one of the host sulfides in which fine gold is disseminated and from which gold can be recovered by flotation.

nodes.name: Autoclave Leaching of Sulfide Gold Concentrates
nodes.definition: Hydrometallurgical opening of finely disseminated gold in sulfide concentrates by oxygen-assisted pressure leaching in an autoclave. The method oxidizes pyrite and arsenopyrite under acidic or alkaline conditions, leaving the liberated gold in the solid residue for subsequent cyanidation.
